- `js/weapon.js:520-527` — `willWeld()`, pre-existing, with `erodeable_wep()`
  inlined into it, reached from `mwelded()`.

Both are live. The bodies agree today: weapon class or weptool or heavy iron
ball or iron chain, cursed, or a tin opener. Neither file mentioned the other
until the audit for `aa9f3c85..3b2f83d`, which added a cross-reference comment
at each site as the in-scope half of the fix.

The convergence itself is out of scope for an audit fix, because `js/weapon.js`
is outside that reviewed range and `mwelded()` is live monster code. Resolve it
by exporting `will_weld()` from `js/wield.js`, deleting `willWeld()`, and
pointing `mwelded()` at the survivor, with the development score identical
across the change.

Same shape as `isok-ported-twice`. A simplification pass over these two entries
would settle both.

deferred.id: minliquid-refusal-ignores-flyers
deferred.detail:
`unportedMinliquidReason()` in `js/unported_monster_actions.js:167-168`, and
the sibling test at `:205-206`, refuse on bare `is_pool(...) || is_lava(...)`.
C's `minliquid_core()` derives the two flags with a flyer and floater
exemption:

    inpool = (is_pool(mtmp->mx, mtmp->my)
              && (!(is_flyer(mtmp->data) || is_floater(mtmp->data))
                  || Is_waterlevel(&u.uz)));            /* mon.c:967-970 */
    inlava = (is_lava(mtmp->mx, mtmp->my)
              && !(is_flyer(mtmp->data) || is_floater(mtmp->data)));

So a flying or floating monster over water or lava is left alone by C, and
refused by the port. A bat crossing a pool ends the segment where C simply
continues the turn.

The refusal is fail-closed, so it cannot produce a wrong screen or a wrong
random number; what it costs is replay length, and replay length is screens.
That makes it a scoring cost rather than a correctness defect, which is why the
gremlin slice at `3249e2d` documented it in place rather than narrowing it.

Narrowing it means porting the arms it stands in for: the drown effect at
`mon.c:1068` and the burn effect at `:1010`, with `is_flyer()` and
`is_floater()` first. Resolve this entry when those land, or earlier if a
scored session is measured stopping here on a flyer -- the cheap check is to
count how many development sessions reach a flying or floating monster over
liquid at all.

Found by reading during the `monsters` deferral sweep, not by a failing test.

deferred.id: touch-artifact-ported-but-unwired
deferred.detail:
`js/artifacts.js touch_artifact()` is a complete, tested port of artifact.c
touch_artifact():908's monster branch, and it is pure on that branch:
`badalign && (!yours || !rn2(4))` short-circuits on `!yours`, so a monster
answer draws nothing, prints nothing, and changes no state. 3d33c40 landed it
on 24 July 2026 as a pure-function batch and wired no consumer.
`grep -rn touch_artifact js/` finds it only in js/artifacts.js and in three
comments; no production path has ever called it.

Five injections stand in for it instead, each refusing every artifact its
monster meets: `touchArtifact` at js/unported_monster_actions.js
moveSimpleOrdinary(), refuseHeroAttack(), postMoveRangedAttack() and
wieldMonsterItem(), plus js/monmove.js postmov():2519-2527. They reach
artifactTouchable() (js/artifacts.js, below touch_artifact()), which repeats
only the ART_NONARTIFACT early return and hands every artifact to the
injection. AGENTS.md, "Port pure functions in bulk", says an injection a
ported function replaces is deleted in the same batch; that batch did not,
so the port and its stand-in have coexisted since.

Wiring it strictly reduces refusals and is what C does: an artifact the
monster may not touch is skipped silently rather than stopping the segment.
The slice that found this refused instead, because the other answer opens
live behavior no recording covers - a monster or pet carrying an artifact off
the floor, which runs mpickstuff() -> distant_name() -> xname() ->
find_artifact(), the only writer of artiexist[].found, and a monster wielding
one through mon_wield_item(). Closing this needs a fresh C case with a floor
artifact beside a monster. The scan that found the original crash put a D:1
floor artifact at roughly one seed in twelve thousand, so build the case with
direct wizard-mode setup rather than a seed search.

deferred.id: record-session-signal-test-races
deferred.detail:
`scripts/record-session.test.mjs`, "fails when a complete marker stream ends
with an unexpected signal", races. Its fake recorder writes a complete input
marker to fd 1 with `fs.writeSync(1, marker)` and then immediately runs
`process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGUSR2')`, so the parent's observation of the
marker on the pipe against its observation of the signal death is an ordering
the test does not control.

Observed once on CI during the `monsters-deferral-sweep` artifact-touch slice:
the run reported status 0 where the test asserts 1. It passes locally, and a
re-dispatch of the identical commit passed (run 31129020658, head 6b79b077), so
the failure is load-dependent rather than a defect in the recorder.

A flaky test costs more than the minutes it wastes: it teaches the next agent
to re-run a red suite instead of reading it, which is the habit most likely to
let a real regression through.

The fix is to make the ordering explicit rather than probable -- have the fake
recorder wait for the parent to acknowledge the marker before signalling, or
have the assertion accept either interleaving while still requiring the signal
to be reported. Decide which from `scripts/record-session.mjs`'s own reader,
because only one of those is faithful to what the production path guarantees.

`scripts/` is not area-owned, so this entry carries no area.

deferred.id: wield-placement-and-dead-export
deferred.detail:
Two leftovers from the duplicate-port convergence at `1af25e7`, both found by
reading and neither in scope for that slice.

**`mwelded()` sits in the wrong file.** C owns it at `wield.c:1078`, so
`AGENTS.md` "Keep each source file's port in one place" puts it in
`js/wield.js`; the port has it at `js/weapon.js mwelded()`. The convergence
slice pointed it at the surviving `will_weld()` as its deferral asked and left
the move. The move is cheap now: `js/muse.js` and `scripts/weapon.test.mjs` are
its only importers, and the `js/weapon.js` -> `js/wield.js` import edge already
exists after the convergence. `which_armor()` is the sibling to check at the
same time, since `js/muse.js` imports both from `js/weapon.js` in one
statement.

**`_weaponInternals` is an export nobody imports.** `js/weapon.js` freezes and
exports it; `grep -rn "_weaponInternals" js/ scripts/ tools/` returns only the
definition. The convergence removed the deleted function from the object and
left the object, correctly, because deleting an export is not a rename. It is
either a test seam whose test was rewritten to import the functions directly,
or scaffolding that outlived its purpose; read `scripts/weapon.test.mjs` before
deciding which.

Neither changes behavior. Both are placement and dead-declaration cleanups of
the kind a simplification pass settles, which is why they are one entry rather
than two.

deferred.id: depth-ported-twice-with-differing-bodies
deferred.detail:
`dungeon.c depth()` has two live ports whose bodies **differ**, and one module
imports both:

- `js/dungeon.js depth(level, state = game)` threads `state`. This is the
  correct owner by file name: C defines the function in `dungeon.c`.
- `js/hacklib.js depth(uz)` ignores any state argument and reads the
  module-global `game`. `js/hacklib.js` is the wrong home, the same
  skeleton-leftover shape as the duplicate `isok()` that `1af25e7` converged.

`js/mklev.js` binds both under aliases in separate statements, `depth as
dungeon_depth` from `./dungeon.js` and `depth as depth_of_level` from
`./hacklib.js`, so a reader of either call site sees a plausible name and no
sign that two implementations are in play.

They disagree in three ways. At `js/mklev.js initialize_themeroom_branch()`,
which takes `state = game`, the `depth_of_level` call reads the level from the
passed state and `depth_start` from the module-global `game`. When
`depth_start` is 0 the `hacklib` copy returns `dlevel` through a `|| 1` and the
`dungeon` copy returns `dlevel - 1`. When the dungeon is missing the `hacklib`
copy returns a default and the `dungeon` copy throws.

This is a latent hazard rather than a demonstrated bug: no path was found today
where the passed state differs from the module global. It becomes live the
moment one does, and it will not announce itself, because both copies answer
plausibly.

`1af25e7` converged the two duplicates the ledger happened to record and swept
for no others. Resolve this one the same way -- one owner in `js/dungeon.js`,
`js/mklev.js` repointed, the alias removed -- and confirm an identical
development score, which is the only evidence a behavior-preserving move needs.

deferred.id: end-running-travelmap-two-ports
deferred.detail:
`js/hack.js endRunning()` carries the comment "gt.travelmap has no ported
counterpart, so its selection_free() is absent." That is false, and acting on
it would delete live code.

`grep -rn "travelmap" js/ scripts/` returns exactly two lines: that comment,
and `js/detect.js state.travelmap = null;`. The second sits inside a function
headed "C ref: hack.c nomul(0), including end_running(TRUE)'s state effects",
so it *is* a port of `hack.c`'s travelmap clear.

The defect underneath the comment is that `hack.c end_running()` has two
disagreeing ports. `js/hack.js endRunning()` does not clear `travelmap`; the
copy inside `js/detect.js` does. A reader who trusts the comment concludes the
`detect.js` line is unported scaffolding and removes it.

Resolve by deciding which function owns `end_running()`'s state effects --
`hack.c` names `js/hack.js` -- moving the clear there, having the `detect.js`
path call it, and correcting the comment. Confirm an identical development
score: whichever way the ownership falls, no scored session should observe a
difference today, because the two paths already agree on the value written.

Found by an audit of absence claims across `js/` comments on 6 August 2026.
That audit checked 53 such claims and found 14 false or stale, so this entry is
one instance of a class rather than an isolated slip.

deferred.id: mon-allowflags-and-helpless-placement
deferred.detail:
Two placement leftovers found while closing the last sweep slice at `a448201`.

**`mon_allowflags()` is in the wrong file.** C owns it at `mon.c:2064`, so
`AGENTS.md` "Keep each source file's port in one place" puts it in `js/mon.js`;
the port has it at `js/monmove.js`. It carries a second copy of the
`can_tunnel` clearing that `m_move()` also performs, which is placement only
rather than a duplicate port -- C duplicates it too. Note that the `m_move()`
copy now has seven mutants killed by a dedicated test while this one has no
comparable coverage, so move it with a test rather than without.

**`monst.h:251 helpless()` is ported once and inlined three times.** The port
is `js/mhitm.js helpless()`. Three call sites reimplement its body inline and
cite the same C line rather than importing it: two in `js/steed.js` and one in
`js/dog.js`. The bodies agree today.

The second is the fourth duplicate-port finding of 6 August 2026, after
`isok()`, `will_weld()` and `depth()`. Unlike those it is an inlining rather
than a second definition, so a duplicate-export report would not list it; only
reading finds this shape.

deferred.id: options-config-error-and-parser-residue
deferred.detail:
Four follow-ups found while applying the correctness pass over
`a97c0a1..e9723ab`, none of them in its fourteen findings.

**`count_apes()` carries the identical defect the pass fixed three times over.**
Its comment cites the port's missing `AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION` statement as
evidence that the exception list is empty. `cfgfiles.c` has
`CNFL_N(AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION, 5)`, so C reads such a statement and the port
drops it. Adding a fourth row to `UNPORTED_CONFIG_STATEMENTS` closes it in
about three lines, and it is the same reasoning error: the port's own gap
offered as a fact about the game.

**A boolean written by an unhandled `OPTIONS=<name>:true` is stored as the
string `'true'`.** The options menu now refuses to display it, so the wrong
value cannot reach a screen through that path, but it stays wrong wherever else
it is read.

**`createCommandBindingModel()` does not skip `INTERNALCMD` rows** the way
`cmd.c bind_key()` does, so a binding to an internal command succeeds in the
port and fails in C.

**The port has no non-fatal config error.** `optfn_sortloot()`,
`optfn_versinfo()` and `optfn_msg_window()` all call `config_error_add()` and
let the game continue; the port throws. Matching C there is its own slice, and
it is the shape most likely to cost screens: C keeps playing where the port
stops.

deferred.id: full-screen-menu-dismissal-repaints-status
deferred.detail:
`js/tty_menu.js dismissTtyMenu()` restores a snapshot of the base window where
`wintty.c erase_menu_or_text()` (966-984) calls `docrt(); flush_screen(1)` for a
full-screen menu. The two differ on the rows `docrt()` does not repaint: C's
`cls()` blanks the whole screen, redraws the map, and sets `disp.botlx` so the
status lines come back at the next `bot()`; the port hands the status lines
back immediately, from the snapshot.

Reproduce it with this recipe, which is scripts/run-options-menu.mjs's fifth
with the boolean pick removed from each round, so no message intervenes:

    seed 4210041, datetime 20281114073500,
    nethackrc = the file scripts/run-options-menu.mjs nethackrc([]) builds,
    moves = ' mO     n\r c%\rmO     n\r A\rmO     n\r =\r\x1b'

Expected failure: `node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs --recipe <that file>` reports
`First screen mismatch ... Cell row 23, column 1 (ch): C:" " JS:"O"` at the
boundary where the class menu first draws. PRNG, cursors and every earlier
screen match.

Every path that reaches a second window inside one command without an
intervening message is exposed. Nothing in the development sessions is: each
one that commits an options menu also toggles a boolean, and `ttyPline()`'s
`flush_screen(1)` repaints over the difference before the next screen is
captured. That is also why the defect predates the slice that found it -- until
`handler_pickup_types()` landed, no command opened a second window after a
full-screen menu at all.

Fixing it means giving the port a `bot_disabled`-shaped notion of a status line
that is blank until the next `bot()`, which is the same machinery
`flush_screen() rebuilds the whole screen` needs; read that entry first.

deferred.id: object-predicates-ported-under-mixed-spellings
deferred.detail:
Four `obj.h` object predicates are ported under mixed spellings, and two of
them more than once. Verified at `e593b94`:

- `is_weptool` (obj.h:249) — one port, `js/obj.js:673 isWeptool`, exported.
- `is_missile` (obj.h:245) — one port, `js/worn.js:390 is_missile`, exported.
- `is_launcher` (obj.h:235) — two ports: `js/worn.js:403 is_launcher`,
  exported under the C name, and `js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js:154 isLauncher`,
  module-private and taking an object *type* rather than an object.
- `is_ammo` (obj.h:238) — **five** ports: `js/obj.js:678` and
  `js/worn.js:384`, both exported as `is_ammo`, plus module-private `isAmmo` at
  `js/startup_skills.js:167`, `js/invent.js:2035` and
  `js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js:158`.

The cost is not only duplication. `AGENTS.md` requires a ported function to
carry its C name, and that rule is what makes a name-shaped search
trustworthy. Where it slipped here, two separate agents grepped the C names,
got zero hits, and concluded the predicates were unported — one of them while
scoping a goal that needs all four for `wield.c:75 TWOWEAPOK`. A third report,
correcting the second, was itself wrong about which spellings exist. Every
reading of this area has so far produced a defensible command and an
indefensible conclusion.

Resolve by converging each predicate on one owner named for its C file --
`obj.h` predicates belong with the objects area -- and deleting the private
copies, confirming an identical development score, which is the only evidence a
behavior-preserving move needs. Check the bodies before merging: the
`u_init_inventory_attrs.js` copies take an object type where the others take an
object, so they are not textually interchangeable.

Same shape as `isok-ported-twice` and `will-weld-ported-twice`, both closed by
the monsters sweep, and as `depth-ported-twice-with-differing-bodies`, still
open.

notes.text:
Correction to this entry's `is_launcher` line, and to the reasoning in the
commit that opened it.

That line was written from the working tree while the `twoweapon-command` slice
held it mid-edit, so it described the slice's uncommitted change as if it were
pre-existing state. At `5dd14ef`, before the slice landed, `js/worn.js:401` was
module-private `isLauncher`; `e4d15db` renamed and exported it as
`is_launcher` at :403. The line reads true at the current head only because the
slice made it true.

That inverts the attribution in the opening commit. It said a report correcting
the "unported" claim was itself wrong about which spellings exist. It was not:
the goal-selector's account -- both `is_launcher` ports module-private and
camelCase -- was correct for the tree as it then stood, and the orchestrator's
correction of it was the error. The slice worker caught this and said so.

The entry's substance is unaffected. `is_ammo` still has five live ports, one
per file in `js/obj.js`, `js/worn.js`, `js/startup_skills.js`, `js/invent.js`
and `js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js`, re-counted from the committed head rather
than the working tree. `is_launcher` now has two, one of them exported under
its C name. The convergence this entry asks for is unchanged.

The transferable lesson is about method, not this area: while a worker holds
the working tree, verify a claim about repository state against a committed
ref -- `git show <sha>:<path>` -- because a plain grep reads a mutating tree
and cannot tell an in-flight edit from history.

deferred.id: doname-twoweap-guard-too-broad
deferred.detail: js/objnam.js:264 refuses doname() for ANY worn object once u.twoweap is set: 'if (obj.owornmask && state.u?.twoweap) unsupported("two-weapon suffix", obj)'. objnam.c doname_base() reads u.twoweap in exactly two places, at :1562 for W_WEP (twoweap_primary picks "wielded in" over "weapon in") and at :1614 for W_SWAPWEP ("wielded in left hand" over "alternate weapon; not wielded"). deferred.id: walltalk-clamp-unpinned-until-hallucination
deferred.detail:
js/sounds.js:351 clamps rn2(10) to WALLTALK's 8 entries inside dochat()'s hallucinating wall reply, ported verbatim from sounds.c:1366-1367. Mutating >= to > is a real behavior change, not an equivalence: idx reaches 9, so an idx of 8 escapes the clamp and the reply prints "The wall undefined". The mutant survives only because Hallucination(state) cannot be true. The direct proof is that `grep -rnE "\[HALLUC\]\s*(\.\s*(intrinsic|extrinsic|blocked)\s*)?=[^=]|set_itimeout|incr_itimeout|make_hallucinated" js/` returns no assignment: all HALLUC references in js/ are reads.

This turns into a live defect the first time make_hallucinated() gains a writer, and sessions/seed0383-wizard-hallucinate.session.json is already recorded against that day. Whoever ports a hallucination source should pin this clamp with a test at the same time.

deferred.id: chat-no-answer-arms-refused-as-one
deferred.detail:
sounds.c dochat() holds four arms between the wall block and domonnoise() that js/sounds.js:365 refuses as one: the M_AP_FURNITURE and M_AP_OBJECT disjuncts at :1374-1377, the helpless-monster "%s seems not to notice you." at :1380-1386, the tame-and-meating "%s is eating noisily." at :1391-1396, and the Deaf "Any response%s%s %s." at :1397-1407. The clearing of mtmp->mstrategy's STRAT_WAITMASK at :1389 sits among them. A return-by-return audit of all 17 returns above :1408 found these the only shortfall; every other arm is ported and every excluded call refuses before output, randomness, or state change, so the port is fail-closed here rather than wrong.

They belong with domonnoise() rather than with the chat-command goal, for three reasons. They move no development session: eight sessions record ten #chat commands, and the only one landing on an unported in-boundary arm is seed0004-feeding-pony step 346, in a session that halts at screen 26 of 409 on a bear trap at step 27. The eating arm cannot fire at all, because meating's three writers in js/ all write 0 and its C writer dogmove.c dog_eat() :166-210 is unported, so no fresh differential can exercise it until that lands. And the three live arms need canspotmon(), Monnam() and mon_nam() under the same conditions domonnoise() needs them, so porting them separately splits one slice in two.

Whoever takes them should know four things. :1389 gives chat its first state write, feeding js/monmove.js:1861, so a differential must run several turns past the reply rather than stopping at it. js/do_name.js:127-128 records that mon_nam() and Monnam() cover an early ordinary-monster subset, missing invisibility, mimic appearance and the peaceful and tame adjectives; canspotmon() guards both new call sites, which removes the unseen cases but not a sleeping peaceful or invisible target. map_invisible() at :1393 is reachable only inside the dead eating arm's !canspotmon sub-branch, and porting it arms the throw at js/display.js:1530, so leave it refused. The Deaf format string at :1402-1405 passes canspotmon(mtmp) twice, so one stray space is a full screen mismatch.

The helpless-steed arm at :1297-1300 returns ECMD_TIME above domonnoise() at :1302 and is refused by the same reading. It needs a mounted hero, an asleep or immobilized steed, and a downward chat, which "Complete common gameplay first" defers.

The generated CMAP_EXPLANATIONS entry for S_web held "',  S_web, " because the extractor scanned the whole entry for its last quoted string and that entry's character literal is a double quote.
objnam.c just_an() was ported twice in js/objnam.js.
vtense()'s es and s branches appended lowercase literals where C writes them through Strcasecpy(), dropping case propagation.
dfeature_at() read the door mask as doormask||flags, reversing the precedence every other reader in the port uses.

UnsupportedMonsterCreationError is converted only on the cloned planning round, so for an unencumbered hero the live maybe_generate_rnd_mon() refusal escapes runSegment() rather than ending the segment at a boundary. The pet-swap probe run against the parent tree returned the same swaps as at 03c2add for seeds 777, 5150, 840004, 31009 and 1234 (e.g. `31009 RETURNED hero [ 63

passes.head: 60bf2c3cf1fc8d7313970a91417547af466206c3
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the no-time-command goal: dodiscovered(), dospellmenu(), doattributes() and enlightenment(), plus weapon_descr()'s move into js/weapon.js. Four finders ran (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency were not enabled, because the range adds no hot-path work and no new shared mutable state. 17 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, 14 confirmed and all 14 applied across 7d11c53 and 2adc5af; 2 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. The four production defects were Fixed_abil read as intrinsic-or-extrinsic, a stop on every wielded towel rather than a wet one, a deafness guard that missed u.uroleplay.deaf, and can_advance() refusing on speedy ahead of the three tests C answers FALSE from. Validation at 2adc5af: 1,765 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 98,759 PRNG values and 286 screens and cursors with no session regressed, and the no-time matrix matching 71,967 calls with 158 screens and cursors across 29 segments.

productionDefects.summary: one_characteristic() tested Fixed_abil through hasProperty(), which ORs the intrinsic and the extrinsic. youprop.h:385 defines the macro as the extrinsic alone, with no HFixed_abil term, so an intrinsic in that slot stopped the command where C prints the six characteristics.

weapon_insight() refused every wielded towel, but obj.h defines is_wet_towel(o) as otyp == TOWEL && spe > 0 and weapon.c lists TOWEL among weapon_descr()'s P_NONE overrides, so a dry towel prints "You are wielding a towel."

The deafness guard read u.uprops[DEAF] only, but youprop.h:245 defines Deaf as (HDeaf || EDeaf || u.uroleplay.deaf). OPTIONS=deaf sets the third term alone, so the port printed a window where C prints " You are deaf."

can_advance() refused on speedy before evaluating the three tests C answers FALSE from, so a restricted or maxed skill ended the segment instead of answering FALSE. C's shortcut is wizard && speedy and sits after those tests.

rejections.summary: status_enlightenment() accepts mode and never reads it, said to hide that C's `boolean magic = (mode & MAGICENLIGHTENMENT)` gate on the Fumbling, Sleepy and Hunger arms was replaced by unconditional stops.
rejections.counterEvidence: insight.c:728 declares basics_enlightenment(int mode UNUSED, int final), so upstream itself carries an unread mode on a section function and mirroring the C signature is the faithful choice; the port also threads mode to one_characteristic(), which reads it. The over-broad stops fail closed for states no supported path can produce, so no screen, message or random-number call differs from the C. The proposed lint check would equally flag a faithful port of insight.c:728. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that makes an unread mode change output.

rejections.summary: None of js/insight.js's 16 stops is exercised by any test, and the fail-closed property is said not to hold because 12 of the 16 run after basics_enlightenment() has called find_ac().
rejections.counterEvidence: find_ac()'s write is conditional on armorClass !== u.uac, matching do_wear.c:2508-2510 at the same point in the same sequence, and js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js is untouched by the reviewed range. Measured on a live game at a ready D:1 prompt, u.uac and disp.botl read the same before and after an extra find_ac() call, so no stop leaves state the prompt did not already have; C calls find_ac() before the same points regardless. The residual true claim, that no test threw a stop, was addressed separately: the applied fixes add tests that throw the towel, stuck_ring() and deafness stops. Do not reopen without a state where find_ac() writes before a stop and the write is observable.

passes.head: 2adc5af64b2a6dffc08e56c1ae71d0b453f92d73

The rejected finding, a real Deaf mismatch in js/dogmove.js, is outside the range and unreachable, and is recorded in ROADMAP.md for the leashed-pet work. Validation at acf05a3: 1,767 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 98,759 PRNG values with 286 screens and cursors, and the no-time matrix matching 71,967 calls with 158 screens across 29 segments.

rejections.summary: js/dogmove.js heroDeaf() reads u.uprops[DEAF] alone and adds a `blocked` term youprop.h:125 has no counterpart for, so OPTIONS=deaf was said to still diverge in dogmove.c's leashed-pet trap arm.

passes.head: 60bf3d04c84bce48ff7aadf7989556874ee0f3e5
passes.evidence: Full pass over the whole running and rushing goal: the room run, corridor running, and ctrl-direction rush, plus the runmode option and the animation-frame comparison stream. Four finders ran (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency were not enabled, because the range adds no hot-path work beyond the source-required per-turn traversal and no new shared mutable state. 16 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, 13 confirmed: 7 applied at 374fb85 and 6 deferred, 3 rejected with counter-evidence, 0 unverified, 0 warnings. Both production defects were applied. The first is the one that mattered: endRunning() dropped the disp.time_botl set and terrainstatus recompute that hack.c:4132-4145 performs, while the port had already ported the two places that suppress those updates during a run, so the catch-up had no owner. The six deferred findings are all missing test pins rather than suspected wrong behavior, each naming a mutation the suite survives; they are recorded in ROADMAP.md with the instruction to clear them before the next holdout, and two of them need a fresh C recording with mention_walls set. Validation at 374fb85: 1,800 tests passing, four generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, development score unchanged at 99,496 PRNG values and 321 screens with all 33 sessions identical, and all three run matrices matching 90,877, 87,714 and 57,676 PRNG calls with 115, 126 and 61 screens and 325, 268 and 163 animation frames.

productionDefects.summary: endRunning() implemented two of end_running()'s four responsibilities, dropping the disp.time_botl set and the terrainstatus recompute that hack.c:4132-4145 performs inside its `if (svc.context.run)` guard. moveloop_core() and classify_terrain() suppress both updates for the whole of a run so this function can make them up; the port had the suppressing halves without the catch-up. nomul() masked it by setting disp.botl itself, but the direct callers in js/uhitm.js and js/eat.js reach endRunning() without nomul.

curs_on_u() took no state and flushed the module-global game, so runmode_delay_output(state) wrote disp.time_botl into one object while flush_screen()/bot() read and cleared it from another. Production always passes game, so the mismatch was reachable only from a test, and the existing test hit it silently. curs_on_u() now refuses a non-global state and the test drives the real object.

rejections.summary: interrupt_multi() was said to emit its boundary before nomul(0), reversing allmain.c's statement order, with the comment justifying the reversal on the wrong ground.
rejections.counterEvidence: Refuted against the source order in allmain.c; the reviewers' own verification could not sustain the claimed reversal as a behavioral difference. Do not reopen without a recorded case where the emitted boundary and the nomul(0) produce a different observable order.

rejections.summary: endRunning() was said to zero a positive multi, which end_running(TRUE) never does, making it an invented clamp now live on do_attack()'s 'is in the way' path.
rejections.counterEvidence: The central factual claim is false. hack.c:4153-4156 is `/* cancel multi */ if (gm.multi > 0) gm.multi = 0;`, the closing statements of end_running(), so the port's clamp is a faithful translation. The line is also pre-existing: `git show 2adc5af:js/hack.js` already contains it, and the diff shows it only as context. The proposed fix would introduce the divergence it claims to remove. Do not reopen without a C reading that contradicts hack.c:4153-4156.

rejections.summary: totalFrames() in scripts/diff-fresh.mjs duck-types two element shapes, the C side's {frames, location} objects and the JS side's bare arrays, behind `(step.frames ?? step).length`.
rejections.counterEvidence: Judged not to survive verification as a defect in this range. Do not reopen without a recorded case where the two shapes yield a different frame total than a shape-explicit reading would.

passes.head: f826ba5392d313da8951095111b8201f5be497fe
passes.evidence: Full pass over the extended-command prompt, which fired the commands gate at 1,289 of 1,000 unreviewed lines. Four finders ran; performance and concurrency were not enabled. 19 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, all 16 confirmed and none rejected. Four are applied at 2640c9f: three production defects and the generated-table test that pins the restored column. Twelve are deferred, and three of those are one defect seen from three angles — the port's flush_screen() is a whole-screen rebuild where display.c's re-emits only dirty cells, so the faithful vpline() flush_screen(1) call this range added erases an open tty menu at the two pre-existing menu-search call sites. .agents/review.md puts that outside audit-fix scope, because it changes rendering behavior and needs the gnew dirty discipline and gb.bot_disabled, which the port lacks; it is recorded in ROADMAP.md with the instruction to implement it and then run a new full pass over the expanded range rather than a delta. This pass does not cover that implementation. The applied fixes: tty_get_ext_cmd() had dropped C's iflags.extmenu guard entirely and the option was parsed and discarded, so a path meant to fail closed gave the typed prompt; a 0xFF byte was stored as text where C's signed char cast makes it EOF and cancels the line; and the generated table had dropped extcmdlist[]'s f_text column, which rhack() reads to name a counted command's occupation. Validation at 2640c9f: 1,808 tests passing, five generated-data checks including check:extcmds, check:namespace-members, development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 PRNG values, and the matrix matching 71,359 calls with 370 screens plus 12,261 calls with 33 screens in debug mode.

productionDefects.summary: tty_get_ext_cmd() dropped C's first statement, `if (iflags.extmenu) return extcmd_via_menu();`, replacing it with a comment. Nothing read the option at all: parseNethackrc accepted `extmenu` and discarded it, so a deliberately unported path did not fail closed and silently gave the typed prompt instead.

A 0xFF input byte was stored as ordinary text. cmd.c:452 ends pgetchar() with `return (char) ch;` and char is signed, so 255 arrives as -1 and getline.c:85 treats it as EOF, cancelling the line and setting iflags.term_gone. The restart arm is gated on Escape alone, so EOF cancels even over existing text.

The generated extcmdlist[] table dropped the sixth column, f_text, which rhack() reads at cmd.c:3728 to name the occupation a counted command starts. 'search' and 'wait' are the two rows carrying one, and neither the file nor the generator said a column was missing.

hooked_tty_getlin()'s new flush_screen(1) erases an open tty menu, because the port's flush_screen() is a whole-screen rebuild through _buildScreenOutput() while display.c's re-emits only dirty glyph-buffer cells and select_menu() sets gb.bot_disabled. The call itself is faithful to pline.c vpline(); the function it calls is not.
The two pre-existing ttyGetlinSearch menu call sites now run the new unconditional flush_screen(1) and are untested against the menu erasure it causes.

hooked_tty_getlin() ports pline.c vpline()'s `if (u.ux) flush_screen(...)` without the `state === game` guard that the other port of the same C line carries, so a non-global state would flush the wrong game.

passes.head: 4e9a59f8b7098a4f9e80e7d05c7df2bc21363071
passes.evidence: Light delta review of the audit-fix and debt-clearing tail behind the extended-command pass. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability skipped, which the clarity audit covers. 8 raw findings, 6 after deduplication, 5 confirmed. All five applied in 61f41f9: extmenu added to HANDLED_BOOLEAN_OPTIONS so every spelling options.c:5224 accepts reaches iflags; getline.c:120 corrected to getline.c:85 and cmd.c:102 to cmd.c:3728; six tests pinning the EOF gate and the extmenu guard, each verified by applying a mutation and watching it fail. Suite 1,823 passing, up from 1,817. Development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 random-number values across 33 sessions; the extended-command matrix unchanged at 31 segments and 71,392 calls plus 4 debug segments and 12,261 calls.

productionDefects.summary: applyBooleanOption() gained an extmenu arm but HANDLED_BOOLEAN_OPTIONS did not gain the name, so OPTIONS=extmenu:true fell through to the compound-option path: iflags.extmenu stayed undefined and the raw string was parked in flags. options.c:5224 maps true, yes, on and 1 to not-negated for any boolean, so C ran extcmd_via_menu() where the port opened the typed prompt. The fail-open the arm was added to close stayed open for one of the three spellings.

rejections.summary: The correctness finder filed the missing tests for the EOF gate and the extmenu guard a third time as one correctness defect anchored at js/getline.js:176.
rejections.counterEvidence: The anchor line is correct and the finder's own probes say so: '.#wa\xFF' ends with term_gone 1, '.#wa\x00' restarts to '#', and the text concedes 'the gap is validation, not behavior'. js/getline.js:176 reads `if (c !== EOF_BYTE && text)`, which matches getline.c:88's `if (c == '\033' && obufp[0] != '\0')` because only Escape and EOF reach the arm. Its two mutations are identical to ones already carried by the confirmed test findings at js/getline.js:169 and js/getline.js:278. Do not reopen without a divergence at this line that the confirmed test findings do not already cover.

passes.head: 61f41f9b8255ad5359d491196bde97d69ea7d3eb
passes.evidence: Light delta review of the audit-fix tail 61f41f9 together with 671c4fb, the recorder change that sits between it and the previous frontier. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability skipped. 9 raw findings, 7 after deduplication. The workflow confirmed six; the orchestrator rejected one of those on counter-evidence the adjudicator lacked, namely that the range spans two commits and the recorder feature it treats as bundled is 671c4fb's own fully described commit. Five applied in 2ac43bc: extmenu's Off default stored to match optlist.h:303, a third wrong C citation corrected in two files, the tracker test decoupled from live ROADMAP.md prose, and the recorder's own gate given a test through an injectable tracker read. Every fix verified by mutation. Suite 1,824 passing. Development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 random-number values across 33 sessions; all four matrices unchanged.

productionDefects.summary: js/options.js left iflags.extmenu out of the default state while every other Off-defaulting iflags boolean is stored as an explicit false: eight_bit_tty (optlist.h:300), hilite_pet (365), hilite_pile (368), hitpointbar (379) and altmeta (159). optlist.h:303 binds extmenu to &iflags.extmenu with a default of Off, so C's startup value is FALSE rather than absent. The difference is invisible to the truth test in tty_get_ext_cmd() but visible in the second-turn state snapshot, where it is the single differing path across all seventeen cases.

rejections.summary: The correctness finder reported that 61f41f9 bundles an unreviewed recorder feature (deferral validation in scripts/quality-status.mjs plus policy edits) that its commit message never mentions, violating the rule that an audit-fix commit is limited to corrections for confirmed findings.
rejections.counterEvidence: The premise mistakes the range for the commit. `git log --oneline 4e9a59f..61f41f9` lists two commits, and `git show --stat 61f41f9` touches only QUALITY.json, js/getline.js, js/options.js, scripts/generate-extcmds.mjs and the two test files. The recorder feature belongs to 671c4fb, a separate commit whose message describes it in full. The range spanned both because the orchestrator chose it that way, so there is nothing to split. The residual concern, that 671c4fb was never independently reviewed, is answered by this pass covering it: two of its confirmed findings came from that commit and both were applied. Do not reopen without showing that a single commit bundles work outside its stated findings.
rejections.reopenIf: a single commit is shown to bundle work outside its stated findings

rejections.summary: The variable-trace finder reported that the deferral requirement is enforced only at record time, so the 21 already-stored deferred findings across five passes keep no durable record permanently.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator refuted both causality and resolution. The gap predates the range: `git show 4e9a59f:scripts/quality-status.mjs` shows validateAuditMetrics() taking only requireRejections, so no pass carried a deferrals array and no mechanism to require one existed; the change adds a record for future passes and leaves the historical state as it found it. The proposed backfill is also impossible for the majority of the data it targets, because the commit message records that nine of the twelve findings deferred by the extended-command pass existed solely in session-scoped output under /tmp, which is gone. Do not reopen without a recoverable source for the historical deferrals.

passes.head: 2ac43bceb22c833fb670117105f40f85d334cd13
passes.evidence: Light delta review of the audit-fix commit 2ac43bc. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability skipped. 7 raw findings, 5 after deduplication. No production defect: every finding concerns the previous commit's own collateral. The workflow confirmed four and rejected one; the orchestrator promoted that rejection to confirmed and applied it, because the indentation probe it named genuinely certified a CommonMark divergence the test never exercised. All five applied in a010008, which touches test files only. The substantive finding is that storing extmenu's Off default drained the negated-spelling assertions: a mutation stopping the negation arm from writing iflags left all 1,824 tests passing, and failed before the default was added. Each fix verified by mutation. Suite 1,824 passing; development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 random-number values across 33 sessions; the extended-command matrix unchanged.

passes.head: d1a71f7ea035fe6f21567fe7760416ce9b0b5674
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the explicit search command and the debt accumulated in eight areas. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 13 raw findings, 13 after deduplication, 9 confirmed, 7 applied at c706db8, 2 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 4 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. Two applied production defects were reachable and wrong: M_AP_TYPE() dropped monst.h:73's mask, and the statue-trap and hallucinatory-trap refusals threw a bare Error that escaped runSegment() instead of converting to the retryable command boundary. Neither moved a development session, which is why the fresh matrix and the new end-to-end boundary case are the gate rather than the score. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 433 of 7,765 screens and 99,552 PRNG calls; scripts/run-explicit-search.mjs matches 13 segments, 35,560 PRNG calls, 80 screens and 80 cursors; 1,857 tests, four generated-data checks and check:namespace-members pass at c706db8. Every new test was observed failing against the line it covers, each mutation named in that commit message. The range base is the oldest frontier among the claimed areas, so it re-reads commits already covered for the later ones; it also absorbs 88e2193, the previous pass's audit-fix commit, which had been correctness debt since.

productionDefects.summary: M_AP_TYPE() dropped monst.h:73's & M_AP_TYPMASK, so a monster carrying M_AP_F_DKNOWN with no appearance type read as truthy and the explicit search refused a square where C takes mfind0()'s else arm and calls newsym(). The search slice was the helper's first and only consumer.

The explicit search's statue-trap and hallucination exclusions refused with a bare Error instead of UnsupportedSearchError, so failClosedCommand() did not convert them and the refusal escaped runSegment() as a hard failure rather than the retryable command boundary every other exclusion in the slice uses. Reproduced end to end against the live s key.

The same defect traced from preflightTrap(): requireOperation() and requireInjected() raise a bare Error for the statue-trap and hallucination arms, which none of the nine Unsupported* classes failClosedCommand() recognises matches, so the checklist's claim that these exclusions fail closed did not hold at the command boundary. Recorded separately because the variable-trace finder reached it from the throw site rather than from the command path.

js/cmd.js held a second definition of the four hack.h ECMD_* codes while js/detect.js built dosearch()'s return from the js/const.js copy, so the producer and the consumer of that value read different tables.

rhack()'s new search arm applied two of the three result tests cmd.c:3810-3818 applies, omitting the ECMD_CANCEL|ECMD_FAIL test, while its comment claimed parity with the '#' arm. The two forms disagree for (ECMD_TIME|ECMD_CANCEL), the combined result cmd.c:3805-3809 documents by name.

hack.c nomul() has two JavaScript owners: the faithful js/hack.js nomul(), added at 0d4a4ac inside this range, and js/detect.js's older inline defaultNomulZero(), which omits end_running()'s disp.time_botl write and its iflags.terrain_typ/classify_terrain() catch-up. dosearch0() calls the second on its secret-door and secret-corridor finds.

deferrals.summary: hack.c nomul() has two JavaScript owners: the faithful js/hack.js nomul(), added at 0d4a4ac inside this range, and js/detect.js's older inline defaultNomulZero(), which omits end_running()'s disp.time_botl write and its iflags.terrain_typ/classify_terrain() catch-up. dosearch0() calls the second on its secret-door and secret-corridor finds.
deferrals.trackedIn: `nomul()` has two owners and they disagree

deferrals.summary: snapshotMfndposMutation()'s per-slot poss/info snapshot and restore are provable no-ops, because resetMfndposData() reassigns both arrays before the core writes anything, and the comment above them justifies the work with a caller state the same commit made impossible. The rollback test cannot distinguish their removal.
deferrals.trackedIn: the mfndpos rollback restores what nothing changed

rejections.summary: Two comments introduced with runSearchCommand() were said to miscount the command wrappers in opposite directions.
rejections.counterEvidence: Only one half is true. The wrapper definitions sit at js/cmd.js:598, 620, 647, 667, 690 and 695, so 'the five wrappers above' was indeed off by one and has been corrected to four. But the section header's 'the first five wrappers' reads against the handler list its own preceding sentence enumerates -- ddoinv(), dovspell(), dodiscovered(), doattributes(), dolook() and dosearch() -- and is right as written. The finding was stated as two miscounts of which 'neither is right', and that compound claim is false. Do not reopen the header without quoting the sentence two lines above it.

rejections.summary: preflightSearchMonster()'s doc comment was said to claim that a refusal from it always precedes the loop's first rnl(), while one of its two call sites is mfind0(), which runs inside the loop.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment names the dependency the finding says is missing: js/detect.js:530-537 reads 'mfind0() calls this at the square it is looking at and preflightExplicitSearch() calls it at all eight, so a refusal here always happens before the loop's first rnl().' The 'so' clause is derived from the all-eight call site, and the conclusion is true because preflightExplicitSearch() runs to completion before dosearch0() reaches its loop. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that refuses inside the loop and not in the preflight.

rejections.summary: A duplicate of the bare-Error refusal defect, adding that the refusal is mislabelled to the player-facing log as 'automatic search requires ...' and that a doc comment twenty lines above asserts the opposite.
rejections.counterEvidence: The underlying class mismatch is real and is recorded as an applied production defect above; this entry's two distinguishing claims are not. requireOperation() puts that text in an Error that reaches no window: js/cmd.js discards it into an UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError message when it converts, and js/jsmain.js rethrows it otherwise. Nothing routes it through ttyPline(), ttyNorep(), the status line or the top line. Do not reopen the player-facing half without naming the window call that prints it.

rejections.summary: glyph_is_invisible()'s invisible_monster marker was said to be not merely dormant but unimplementable, because remembered_glyph_from_presentation() is the port's sole builder of remembered glyphs and structurally cannot carry it.
rejections.counterEvidence: display.c:378-385 map_invisible() writes levl[x][y].glyph = GLYPH_INVISIBLE directly, routing through no presentation conversion, so a faithful port writes the marker straight onto location.remembered_glyph. That the field is writable is demonstrated in the tree: scripts/detect.test.mjs sets remembered_glyph = { invisible_monster: true } and glyph_is_invisible() answers true, which the same test asserts. Do not reopen without showing that the direct write is unavailable.

passes.head: c706db8a6f372d28630d0f8e9bb06eba929a1123
passes.evidence: Light delta review of c706db8, the audit-fix commit for the e30ea05..d1a71f7 correctness pass, run because an audit-fix commit is correctness debt and the goal's holdout evaluation is a review deadline. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability is the perspective a light pass drops. 8 raw findings, 5 after deduplication, 5 confirmed, 5 applied at 5dd04b2, none deferred, none rejected, none unverified, no warnings. No production defect: every finding is collateral from the fixes themselves, which is what this kind of review is for. The material one is that the new end-to-end statue-trap case could not distinguish a refusal decided before dosearch0's loop from one decided inside it, the single invariant the search slice rests on, because no square in that hero's 3x3 draws any rnl(). The fixture now places a secret door on the first square the traversal visits, and relocating the refusal into the loop with an unchanged class and message was observed failing the case. A screen-count assertion beside it was a tautology against an append-only array and is replaced by the sibling case's oracles. One ROADMAP.md tracking note under-counted the writers of vision_full_recalc and now points at the grep instead. Development score identical to d1a71f7 and c706db8 at 433 of 7,765 screens and 99,552 PRNG calls; 1,857 tests, four generated-data checks and check:namespace-members pass at 5dd04b2.

passes.head: 5879bed71b42deb7fe8346e75e589c42922d956b
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the first slice of the closed-door goal. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 16 raw findings, 15 after deduplication, 13 confirmed, all 13 applied at cfbc205, none deferred, 2 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. Three live production defects: flags.autoopen was never registered as a boolean option so autoopen:false stored a truthy string and defeated the new refusal gate; requireAutoopenClosedDoor() read a state.context.run the admission seam had not yet assigned, so a rush into a closed door committed its movement intent before being refused; and the portcullis guard re-implemented dbridge.c is_drawbridge_wall() without its DB_DIR test, refusing a door whose neighbouring drawbridge faces away. Five test findings were assertions that could not fail, including a refusal-term matrix covering one of six terms and a replay oracle that checked only a screen count. Every new test was observed failing against a named mutation, listed in the fix commit. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 436 of 7,765 screens, 437 cursors and 99,541 PRNG calls; scripts/run-closed-door-autoopen.mjs matches 10 segments, 27,136 PRNG calls, 33 screens and 33 cursors, and the rush matrix 32 segments and 100,341 calls. The range base is the oldest frontier among the claimed areas, so it re-reads the two search audit-fix commits already covered for commands, runtime and world-effects.

productionDefects.summary: flags.autoopen was never registered in HANDLED_BOOLEAN_OPTIONS, so the `autoopen:value` form fell through to the compound-option preservation path and stored the string "false"/"no"/"off" in flags. requireAutoopenClosedDoor() tests `!state.flags.autoopen` and a non-empty string is truthy, so the port pulled at a door options.c:5229-5233 requires C to refuse.

requireAutoopenClosedDoor() read state.context.run, which js/cmd.js assigns only after calling the admission preflight, so the run test was dead at the seam. A rush or run into a closed door was admitted there and refused only inside domove(), after the movement intent had committed.

The same stale-state defect traced from the call site: preflightDomoveDestination() already threads `run` for runStopsBeforeMonster() but dropped it when calling the closed-door guard. Recorded separately because the variable-trace finder reached it from the caller rather than from the guard.

The portcullis guard re-implemented dbridge.c is_drawbridge_wall() inline and omitted its DB_DIR test, refusing a superset: a DOOR whose orthogonally adjacent drawbridge faces away is not a portcullis and C opens it normally. A faithful port of the C function already existed unexported in js/startup_a11y.js.

The comment justifying the deletion of blocksMove()'s door term claimed js/mklev.js never writes loc.doormask for a generated door. dosdoor() does not, but create_door() and the special-level door path do, so the stated premise is false for doors ordinary levels produce; the deletion remains correct for the second reason the comment gave.

The same comment said the closed-door route is now owned "in both callers" when blocksMove() has exactly one caller left, so a reader auditing the deletion could not tell whether the second was removed deliberately or overlooked.

rejections.summary: domove() was said to call test_move() before every monster, attack and terrain branch whereas domove_core() calls it last, with the new comment anchoring the call to the wrong C line.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the ordering claim unsupported against hack.c's actual control flow for this path. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input whose observable output differs because of the claimed ordering, and a diff-causal line.

rejections.summary: The comment on the paired door.flags / door.doormask write was said to claim that every reader in the port accepts either spelling, when readers use the `flags || doormask` idiom.
rejections.counterEvidence: The `flags || doormask` idiom does accept either spelling for every value the port writes, so the comment is accurate as written for the doors this code produces. Do not reopen without a reader that consults only one field and an input that reaches it.

passes.head: cdb83a481180205a8f011ee67b066116a93aaad6
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the second slice of the closed-door goal, the lock.c doopen_indir() message switch. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 17 raw findings, 14 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, all 10 applied at b8323b1, none deferred, 4 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. One live production defect: the seam refused D_LOCKED | D_TRAPPED, a mask lock.c:855 sends through the same message switch as a plain locked door and back out before the trap tail, so the port was refusing a case it fully supports. The second production finding is a premise three comments shared and the C refutes, that closed_door() admits D_LOCKED and D_CLOSED alone; it is a bit test, and the mask guard those comments make look redundant is in fact the only thing keeping a trapped door away from the pull. Six test findings were assertions that could not fail, including two of hack.c:1097's four autoopen terms with no case at all, the drawbridge predicate's vertical arms left unguarded when the range replaced a four-way adjacency check with it, and a replay oracle reading retained message history rather than the rendered line. Every new or changed test was observed failing against a named mutation, each listed in the fix commit. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 442 of 7,765 screens, 443 cursors and 99,625 PRNG calls; scripts/run-closed-door-autoopen.mjs matches 19 segments, 50,018 PRNG calls, 61 screens and 61 cursors. The range also absorbs cfbc205, the previous slice's audit-fix commit, which had been correctness debt since it landed.

productionDefects.summary: The seam refused D_LOCKED | D_TRAPPED as a door whose trap would fire and whose shop would be billed, but lock.c:855 tests only D_CLOSED, so 0x18 enters the same message switch as a plain locked door, prints the same line and returns at :895. The b_trapped() and add_damage() tail at :907-911 is inside the "known to be CLOSED" arm below that return, so the port was refusing a case it fully supports. D_CLOSED | D_TRAPPED stays refused because its roll does reach the tail.

Three comments stated that monmove.c closed_door() admits D_LOCKED and D_CLOSED only. It is a bit test, doormask & (D_LOCKED | D_CLOSED), so D_TRAPPED combinations satisfy it too. The consequence is not merely wording: the mask guard two lines below reads as a restatement of closed_door() when it is the only thing keeping a trapped door away from the pull, and a maintainer deleting it as redundant would let one through to lock.c:904's roll.

rejections.summary: verysmall() and u.usteed were said to be refused ahead of the locked-door arm, where lock.c checks verysmall only after the message switch returns and reads u.usteed inside the kick arm the port already refuses.
rejections.counterEvidence: Neither term can hold in any state the port produces: js/u_init.js initializes usteed to null and no assignment to it exists, and js/mondata.js verysmall() needs msize < MZ_SMALL, which no playable race satisfies while polymorph is unported. The guard lines are also unchanged context in the range's diff. The finding concedes it is latent rather than live. Do not reopen without a source-reachable input that makes either term true.

rejections.summary: The comment above the doopen_indir() call was said to misdescribe how test_move()'s injection contract narrows at the callee.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the described narrowing accurate for the env keys doopen_indir() accepts. Do not reopen without naming a key the caller forwards that the callee neither accepts nor rejects as described.

rejections.summary: Renaming a faithful port of dbridge.c is_drawbridge_wall() to its C name and exporting it from the accessibility-notice module into game logic was said to be the wrong home.
rejections.counterEvidence: The wrong home is real and is stated in a comment at the function, which records that it belongs in a js/dbridge.js port of that file; moving it is a relocation outside audit-fix scope rather than a defect in this range. Do not reopen as a correctness finding; raise it as a simplification trigger instead.

rejections.summary: The dormant-arm test was said to assert result === ECMD_OK for all five masks where C returns ECMD_TIME for one of them.
rejections.counterEvidence: In the state the fixture builds, C returns ECMD_OK for every mask the test drives, because the flags.autounlock arm that produces ECMD_TIME needs a tool the fixture does not supply. Do not reopen without a fixture state in which autokey(TRUE) returns non-null.

passes.head: 4d54fa81d05cc763102b5a17dfc44125325ce46b
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the third and last slice of the closed-door goal, hack.c test_move()'s bump and That-door-is-closed arms. Four mandatory finders (correctness, readability, tests, variable-trace); performance and concurrency not triggered and not enabled. 17 raw findings, 17 after deduplication, 16 confirmed, all 16 applied at 1dc06e8, none deferred, 1 rejected with counter-evidence, none unverified, no warnings. No production defect: the range's own behavior was right. What the pass found was seven test findings and nine comment or citation defects, which matters here more than usual because no development session reaches this arm and the fresh matrix plus the tests are the whole of the evidence. Four assertions could not fail, two of them introduced by the previous cycle's own audit fixes: game.rng?.log?.length compares 0 with 0 because nothing assigns game.rng. The slice's central placement decision - hoisting u.usteed, m_at() and u.utrap above the suppressed-arm early return - was pinned in neither direction, and its mirror case tested two states against a door mask the seam already excludes, so both passed regardless. The silent diagonal arm was pinned only by nothing-observable-happened, and the reviewer's own mutation refusing that arm passed the entire suite; every suppressed segment now asserts its screen count per key and that mutation fails. One guard turned out to be shadowed rather than live: preflightDomoveDestination() tests m_at() before its closed_door() arm, so a monster-occupied door is refused as combat and the door arm's m_at() guard is defensive only. Four C citations pointed at the wrong statement, including a bump gate cited as hack.c:1120, which is exercise(A_DEX, FALSE), and a steed line cited as 1101, which is a comment inside the pull arm. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 442 of 7,765 screens, 443 cursors and 99,625 PRNG calls; scripts/run-closed-door-autoopen.mjs matches 37 segments, 98,012 PRNG calls, 111 screens and 111 cursors. The range also absorbs b8323b1, the previous slice's audit-fix commit, which had been correctness debt since it landed.

rejections.summary: The mask guard was widened to admit D_LOCKED | D_TRAPPED into doopen_indir() without a fresh C recording covering it.
rejections.counterEvidence: The widening was made and validated in the previous range, 5879bed..cdb83a4, not this one, and its basis is a direct source reading: lock.c:855 tests only D_CLOSED, so 0x18 takes the message switch and returns at :895 before the b_trapped() tail. Unit coverage exists in scripts/lock.test.mjs and an end-to-end case pins it in scripts/closed-door-autoopen.test.mjs. Do not reopen without a recorded C case whose behavior differs from the port for that mask.

passes.head: 4d78313de6e5ae5735c531bba8982b089bd2ac00
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the first slice of the pickup goal. Five finders: the four mandatory ones plus performance, enabled because cloneFloorObjects() runs inside a dry run that executes on every elapsed turn; the performance finder confirmed nothing. 19 raw findings, 17 after deduplication, 12 confirmed, 7 applied at 8bd4d6a, 5 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 5 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. Three production defects, two of them in the isolation the slice itself added. The planning dry run wrote the live discovery ledger, because planningState() shared the object catalog, svd.disco and artiexist by spread and cloneFloorObjects() had isolated only the floor; the writes survived even a rejected round. And three refusal classes the new call graph can raise reached the elapsed turn unconverted, so a case that used to stop cleanly on its last matching screen discarded the whole segment. Both are now fixed and pinned, the first by extending the existing atomicity fixture, which could not see the leak until its oracle covered the catalog and u.xray_range forced distant_name()'s near branch. Five test gaps are deferred rather than closed, all of the same shape: the assertion holds whether or not the behavior is present. One further gap is recorded honestly rather than papered over: the refusal-class conversion is pinned on the raising half only, because advanceElapsedTurn() is not exported and the fixture does not reach the arm through moveloop_core(). Development score identical before and after the fixes at 443 of 7,765 screens, 444 cursors and 99,664 PRNG calls; scripts/run-pet-pickup.mjs matches 13 segments, 35,300 PRNG calls, 63 screens and 63 cursors.

productionDefects.summary: The planning dry run wrote the live discovery ledger. distant_name() reaches xname() -> observe_object() -> discover_object(), setting objects[otyp].oc_encountered and svd.disco[], and find_artifact() sets artiexist[].found; planningState() carried all four through its spread, so a dry run mutated live discovery state and the writes survived even a rejected round.

The pickup arm calls distant_name(), splitobj() and mpickobj() from inside the monster scan, so UnsupportedObjectNameError, UnsupportedObjectOperationError and UnsupportedMonsterPickupOperationError can reach the elapsed turn. ELAPSED_TURN_PLANNING_REFUSALS converted none of them and js/jsmain.js rethrows anything else, so a case that used to stop cleanly discarded the whole segment.
The same escape traced from the throw sites rather than the boundary: the slice replaced an injected refusal of a converted class with a call graph raising unconverted ones.

passes.head: 2fea8eb66ad213da5064a8aa49c93f2e9dc5bb67
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over slice 2 of the pickup goal, mpickstuff() and worn.c m_dowear()'s non-creation boundary. Five finders including performance, enabled because the planning clone runs on every elapsed turn. 18 raw findings, 18 after deduplication, 14 confirmed, 3 applied at 292f18c, 11 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 4 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. The three applied are all against the orchestrator's own discovery-ledger fix from 8bd4d6a. The material one is a performance regression that fix introduced: materializing a 482-entry catalog copy on every elapsed turn measured 6.4 ms, which the paired before/after put at 80-92% of a scored turn's total time with identical replay depth on both sides. Object.create() gives the dry run the same isolation for free, because reads delegate to the live entry, a write shadows it on the copy, and the non-enumerable aliases work through the prototype chain since their accessor bodies read this[source]. Removing the line still fails two tests, so the isolation stays pinned. The other two were a vacuous artifact oracle and a comment that overstated which cloned containers are deepened. Of the eleven deferred, one is a production gap — refuseHeroAttack() omits mattacku()'s find_offensive()/use_offensive() path — and five are assertions that do not discriminate, the sharpest being carryamt, which leaves mpickstuff()'s whole split-stack arm disableable with both the suite and the differential green. Development score identical before and after at 443 of 7,765 screens, 444 cursors and 99,664 PRNG calls.

passes.evidence: Light delta review of the pickup goal's audit-fix tail, run because the goal's holdout evaluation is a review deadline and an audit-fix commit cannot stand as correctness debt across one. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability is the perspective a light pass drops. 5 raw findings, 3 after deduplication, 1 confirmed and applied at 14b47f0, none deferred, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. No production defect: the range's twelve production lines, which replaced a materialized catalog copy with Object.create() prototype delegation, hold up. The confirmed finding is collateral from the previous fix and is exactly the class this pass exists to catch: the line added to arm the discovery oracle's artifact third was inert twice over, because artiexist[].found is already zero for every index and the statement sat after the snapshot it was meant to seed, so planningState()'s artiexist clone remained unpinned. The adjudicator traced further than the finder and settled why it cannot be armed from that fixture at all: giving the floor object a real artifact makes can_carry() reach can_touch_safely(), which refuses for a missing touchArtifact operation, so no admitted planning round reaches find_artifact(). passes.head: 005ea20e047e76958b57d78c39ed3136f3ebe1d1
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the slice that gave monmove.c postmov() a home and admitted the inert doorway. Four mandatory finders; performance and concurrency not triggered. 16 raw findings, 13 after deduplication, 11 confirmed, 2 applied at 76659e9, 9 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. Both applied findings are the failure mode the pass was directed at: a call C makes that the port skips, which produces no refusal and no stop. The evacuation of postSimpleMove() out of the boundary file dropped its trap guard on the monster's own square, leaving a monster that reports MMOVE_MOVED without changing square, on a trap, unguarded — the refusal is restored at mintrap()'s own position at monmove.c:1509, reading the live square rather than a destination. And a third silent PRNG gap was found by hunting siblings of the two the slice itself had found: monmove.c:1692-1699 draws rn2(5) for a hides_under() species or an eel, and the pre-scan guard keyed on is_hider(), M1_HIDE, which is a different flag from hides_under(), M1_CONCEAL, so a garter snake, centipede or scorpion reached the arm and the draw was skipped. Of the nine deferred, five are comments stating a false rule about C's door block — its first arm tests D_TRAPPED alone for a magic-key holder and writes the doormask, which is why the port's whole-mask equality is right rather than despite — and four are assertions that do not discriminate. Development score identical before and after the fixes at 446 of 7,765 screens, 446 cursors and 99,840 PRNG calls; scripts/run-monster-doorway.mjs matches 6 segments, 17,436 PRNG calls, 146 screens and 146 cursors.

productionDefects.summary: The boundary evacuation dropped a refusal without replacing it. postSimpleMove() called assertSimpleDestination() for every MMOVE_MOVED, so its trap check covered the monster's own square whether or not the square had changed; postmov() relied on the pre-move gate, which only inspects a square a monster is about to enter, leaving a monster that reports MMOVE_MOVED without changing square, on a trap, with no guard at all.

A third silent PRNG gap: monmove.c:1692-1699 draws rn2(5) for a hides_under() species or an eel with mundetected clear, and helpless() cannot hold because dochug() returns before m_move() for a sleeping or immobile monster. The pre-scan guard keys on is_hider() (M1_HIDE), a different flag from hides_under() (M1_CONCEAL), so a garter snake, centipede or scorpion reached the arm and the draw was skipped with no refusal and no stop.

deferrals.summary: Four copies of the rule that every arm of C's door block tests D_LOCKED or D_CLOSED are false: monmove.c:1543-1548's first arm tests D_TRAPPED alone for a magic-key holder and writes the doormask.
The refusal string for D_ISOPEN | D_TRAPPED names opening a door, an arm that mask cannot reach.
The webmaker comment lists guards C applies that the port does not.

m_move()'s can_tunnel clearing is exercised only in the direction that clears, so every conjunct and the literal 8 survive mutation.

passes.head: 06a5629b044794642e83fd6127cddc7f942680d0
passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the slice that ported monmove.c postmov()'s D_CLOSED door-opening arm and, as its precondition, gave vision_recalc() a state parameter. Five finders including performance, enabled because the cloned scan now owns a terrain grid and vision buffers and the preflight re-derives the transparency index every elapsed turn; the performance finder confirmed nothing. 14 raw findings, 11 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, 2 applied at d7dd150, 8 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 1 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. The material defect was at the seam the pass was pointed at: the transparency-index restore was not side-effect-free, because recalc_block_point() runs rebuildVisionPoint(), which sets vision_full_recalc whenever the change touches the hero's current vision — the normal case for a door in a lit room — so the dry run left a flag the live scan then consumed as a vision_recalc(0) C never performs. The checked-in fixture could not show it, since its viz_array entry at the door is zero and rebuildVisionPoint() takes the other branch; the new test clears the squares between hero and door and recomputes first. The second applied finding is the orchestrator's own from the previous cycle: the trap guard reinstated at monmove.c:1509's position had no test, so deleting it left the whole suite green and the repaired defect could return silently. passes.evidence: Light delta review of the movement-seam ordering fix, run because the monster-door goal's holdout evaluation is a review deadline and audit-fix debt cannot stand across one. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability is the perspective a light pass drops. 8 raw findings, 6 after deduplication, 6 confirmed and all 6 applied at ff865ec, none deferred, none rejected, none unverified, no warnings. This is the fourth consecutive goal in which a delta review found collateral from the previous fix, and this time it found the fix wrong in two ways. Half of it was dead: the refusal guard added for the safemon path was the last statement of its block with nothing after the chain, so deleting it changed no test, while its comment asserted an invariant that did not hold. And moving the pet-swap seam ahead of the refusal made the port throw a segment-ending boundary for a trap or object on the pet's square, on a step C declines without consulting them. The adjudicator settled the question the finder left open by going to the C: uhitm.c:474 evaluates foo = (Punished || !rn2(7) || ...) inside do_attack()'s is_safemon branch, so C spends a draw even for the pet before returning FALSE and letting test_move() refuse — which means neither the original nor the first-fix ordering matched C, and admitting the step silently diverges by exactly one rn2(7). Any monster on a refused diagonal now fails closed, safemon included, ahead of the swap-consequence gates. The pet test asserted the silent refusal and now asserts the boundary plus an unchanged draw count, since failing closed means before the draw rather than instead of it. Three production defects were applied. goto_level()'s Punished guards read state.u.uball where the port owns state.uball, so do.c:1616's refusal failed open, and the test pinning it wrote the same wrong field. flush_screen()'s delay lived in a module variable that an aborted level change latched for the rest of the process, so every later segment would have recorded its cursor at the origin; it now lives on the game state that resetGame() replaces per segment. And failClosedCommandRefusals() omitted four classes the descent handler reaches through goto_level()'s tail, each of which discarded a segment's matching prefix instead of ending it, the same failure the shop slice had just fixed for one other class. Two production defects are deferred: mon_arrive()'s over-wide follower refusal, which needs its own fresh differential, and set_mimic_sym()'s shop arm, which is new upstream work. Validation at the fix commit: 2,325 tests pass, six generated-data checks, check:namespace-members, and the development score unchanged at 488 of 7,765 screens and 106,408 of 610,816 random-number values, every fixed defect being dormant behind a guard no development session reaches. Both new tests were observed failing against the defect they cover. No holdout ran.

productionDefects.summary: goto_level()'s two Punished guards read state.u.uball, where the port's single home for C's global uball is state.uball, the field js/steed.js Punished(), js/insight.js, js/monmove.js, js/steal.js and js/worn.js all read. Both guards were permanently false, so do.c:1616's refusal failed open rather than closed. Both sites now call Punished(), the macro C itself uses at do.c:1616 and do.c:1783. The test that claimed to pin the refusal wrote state.u.uball too, matching the bug, which is why it passed.

flush_screen()'s delay lived in a module variable. C keeps it in a function static and never leaves goto_level() between the two flush_screen(-1) calls; this port can, because nine fail-closed throws sit between them, so an aborted level change latched the flag for the rest of the process and every later segment of the session would have recorded its cursor at the origin. Moved onto the game state, which resetGame() replaces per runSegment().
The same defect reported against the comment asserting that goto_level()'s two flush_screen(-1) calls always balance, when nine throw statements sit between them in the same commit.

failClosedCommandRefusals() omitted UnsupportedPickupError, raised by the pickup(1) that closes goto_level(), so the descent escaped runSegment() as a hard failure and discarded the segment's matching prefix.

The same omission traced end to end across three classes: UnsupportedPickupError, UnsupportedHeroTimeoutBoundaryError from run_timers() and UnsupportedPositionCheckError from mon_arrive() reaching rloc_to(). All three added.
The same omission for UnsupportedMonsterCreationError, which the newly live D:2 shop path raises from inside mklev(). Added to failClosedCommandRefusals(), so the descent ends its segment cleanly.

mon_arrive() at js/dog.js:750 refuses every follower that is neither tame nor u.ustuck, but C's set_apparxy() returns the hero's own square for those monsters too, so the port stops where C continues without drawing a random number. Deferred: deleting a refusal changes what the game does and needs its own fresh differential with a non-tame follower, which no recorded case supplies.

set_mimic_sym()'s rt >= SHOPBASE arm (makemon.c:2467-2480) is unported, so a mimic generated inside the shop mkshop() now places on D:2 raises UnsupportedMonsterCreationError. The class was added to the boundary list so the segment ends cleanly, but porting the arm is new upstream work rather than an audit fix.

productionDefects.summary: js/detect.js:253 was the last surviving reader of state.u.uball, a field nothing in the port writes, so the tactile-floor refusal's two ball-and-chain clauses never fired and it was live only through can_reach_floor().
