js/const.js ismnum() dropped the upper bound of monst.h:285's ((x) >= LOW_PM && (x) < NUMMONS), while js/eat.js kept a faithful private copy: two owners of one macro with the exported one wrong. veggy_item() calls the exported one and then indexes state.mons, so an index at or past NUMMONS answered TRUE and read past the end.

deferrals.summary: mnexto()'s comment in js/teleport.js asserts a complete caller inventory, 'Both ported callers', which omits js/do.js:669 u_collide_m(); the runtime guard that enforced the stand-in's precondition was deleted in the same range, so the comment is now the only statement of it.

scripts/mkroom-shop.test.mjs:524 is the only cover for nameshk()'s shktools arm, and its two assertions leave the name selection itself unpinned; a mutant that keeps the draw but changes which name it returns survives.

Two block headers in scripts/mkroom-shop.test.mjs claim the C differential pins their asserted counts cell for cell because the D:2 map carries one glyph per stocked square, but the recorded D:2 screen contains none of the shop's squares for any of the seeds those blocks use, so the differential does not establish what the headers say.

rejections.summary: That the audit fix replacing u.uball with Punished(state) left two hero-property predicates with incompatible first arguments side by side in js/do.js.
rejections.counterEvidence: The adjudicator found the two predicates take different arguments by design: Punished(state) reads the state root because C's uball is a file-scope object, while heroPropertyActive(u, ...) reads u.uprops because C's property macros are hero fields. The asymmetry mirrors the C source rather than diverging from it. Do not reopen without a source line showing C treats the two alike.

mutation.finderConclusion: 72.7% killed, with relational again weakest at 60%. The run's own baseline was 178 tests in 4 files, a first-wave verdict that under-judges, and scripts/mutate-sites.mjs's header says --whole-suite is not optional at that coverage. The survivors did not drive the pass: its two production defects were both found by reading source, and the most valuable test finding -- that the four refusal classes the previous pass added had no assertion at all -- is invisible to mutation, because deleting a list entry is not an operator mutation. Mutation measured whether the tests pin the lines that exist and said nothing about the line that was wrong.

C's other call site, display.c:340, is already ported at js/display.js:1605-1612 observeNearbyObject(), which uses object_is_generic(), the port of display.h obj_is_generic(), so the helper is never asked C's other question. rejections.summary: The range adds a module-private heroBlind() to js/dungeon.js while js/teleport.js:395 already defines a differently-bodied heroBlind(); the two disagree on whether C's Blind includes u.uroleplay.blind.
rejections.counterEvidence: Both same-named helpers exist, but the half that is wrong is pre-existing and outside this range, and the half this range adds is the C-faithful one: youprop.h:103 defines Blind as ((HBlinded || EBlinded) && !BBlinded) with no uroleplay term, which is what js/dungeon.js:820-824 implements. The range therefore introduces no defect. Do not reopen without a range that touches js/teleport.js:395.

rejections.summary: The range creates an unannotated import cycle between js/steal.js and js/dogmove.js, breaking the repository's convention of naming every cycle and the reason it resolves.
rejections.counterEvidence: The cycle and the missing annotation are real, but the stated hazard cannot occur: both exports at its ends are hoistable function declarations, js/dogmove.js:257 droppables() and js/steal.js:282 relobj(), and ES module linking instantiates function declarations during InitializeEnvironment for every module in the graph before any module body evaluates. What remains is a convention deviation with no failure mode. Do not reopen without a binding in this cycle that is not a hoisted function declaration.

mutation.finderConclusion: The test-quality finder traced the survivor list against source and converted four of it into confirmed findings: both relational survivors at js/const.js:2884 proved that ismnum()'s pm < NUMMONS bound had no test at all, all three logical survivors at js/detect.js:259 proved the same for the tactile-floor guard's ball-and-chain clauses, and the js/steal.js and js/worn.js survivors led to the dknown and silently gaps. The remaining survivors cluster in js/mklev.js (21) and js/do.js (18), on generation constants and on flooreffects() arms whose two answers reach the same named refusal, where no test can observe the difference.

passes.head: 12706a7a5750dbb8b89937511c44c9efc97c9436
passes.evidence: Light delta review over the audit-fix commit, run because .agents/review.md treats the authorized holdout evaluation that follows as a review deadline that audit-fix debt may not cross. Three finders: 12 raw findings, 8 deduplicated, 7 confirmed, 1 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. All seven applied at 8bd0743, with the development score unchanged at 520 of 7,765 screens and 107,227 of 610,816 random-number values. The sharpest was the commit's own production line: see_nearby_objects()'s refusal of a non-global state had no assertion, and deleting the three guard lines left the whole suite green. Two more were the orchestrator's: db386f6's comment cited a .nvmrc this repository does not contain, and correcting the isolation flag's spelling made --focus run every named file in one shared process, where the whole suite reports 2,379 of 2,380.

rejections.summary: The rewritten flooreffects() header states that C's hot-ground potion arm ends with res = TRUE, while do.c:345-353 sets res = TRUE only inside if (!obj_resists(obj, survival_chance, 100)), so a potion that survives the heat leaves res FALSE.
rejections.counterEvidence: The C fact is right but the comment does not claim what the finding attributes to it: do.c:353's res = TRUE is literally the last statement of the arm's body, and the sentence says nothing about the assignment being unconditional. The comment's argument, that porting an arm for real ends the 'unsupported must not return' arrangement and forces else if, holds identically for a conditional assignment. Do not reopen without a reading in which the omitted obj_resists() guard changes what the header asserts about the chain's structure.

mutation.finderConclusion: The range's only js/ change is see_nearby_objects()'s state refusal plus comments, so mutate-sites found no relational, logical or boolean site in scope and produced 0 mutants. The test-quality finder covered that line directly instead, and its confirmed finding is the reason the refusal now has an assertion: it deleted the three guard lines and watched the whole suite stay green.

passes.head: 04c26211d2f0d10bc2277fff1a2fb3aaf9bddc21
passes.evidence: Counts: 11 raw, 10 deduplicated, 6 confirmed, 6 applied, 0 deferred, 4 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 2 survivors of 2 mutants. Full correctness pass over the whole of the experience-level-gain goal: wiz_level_change(), pluslvl(), attrib.c's innate tables with adjabil() and postadjabil(), xlev_to_rank(), add_weapon_skill(), record_achievement(), and the Tourist arrival grant. Five finders including concurrency, enabled because threading a message owner through You_feel() made adjabil() async and rippled to 26 call sites across seven files, among them the new-game initializer every recorded session runs. All six confirmed findings were applied at feac9a2 with the development score unchanged at 648 of 7,765 screens and 107,437 of 610,816 random-number values. The one production defect was scanLevelArgument() returning the full-precision decimal where wizcmds.c:448 declares int newlevel and reads it with sscanf('%d%c'): C converts through strtol() to a long, saturating, then keeps the low 32 bits, so it reads 4294967296 as 0 and any 20-digit answer as -1, while the port raised the hero toward MAXULEV instead. The concurrency finder returned nothing, which is the pass's substantive negative result about the async seam. Recording this pass also surfaced a defect in the recorder: --areas was documented but never parsed, and the summary printed an unbound identifier, so the write succeeded, dropped the field every other pass carries, and then exited non-zero.

optionalFinders.concurrency: enabled: the range converts adjabil() to async, which rippled to 26 call sites across seven files including u_init_misc() and newgame_pre_mklev(), the new-game initializer every recorded session runs
optionalFinders.performance: not enabled: the range adds no unbounded or amplified work, no worse complexity, no hot-path traversal and no startup cost beyond the source behavior it ports

productionDefects.summary: scanLevelArgument() returned the full-precision decimal where wizcmds.c:448 declares int newlevel and reads it with sscanf("%d%c"). glibc converts in two stages, strtol() to a long saturating at LONG_MAX or LONG_MIN and then a store keeping the low 32 bits, so C reads "4294967296" as 0 and any 20-digit answer as -1 while the port read each as itself and raised the hero toward MAXULEV.

mutation.finderConclusion: Both survivors are the saturation guards the audit fix added to scanLevelArgument(): js/wizcmds.js:32 `>` -> `>=` and :33 `<` -> `<=`, each verified against the whole suite of 143 test files and a 2,286-test baseline. Both are equivalent by construction, so no test can kill either: the only input that distinguishes the operators is wide === LONG_MAX (or LONG_MIN), where the guarded body assigns the value the variable already holds. js/display.js contributed no mutable site, its change being a string literal, and the reviewed range's own three survivors were recorded as equivalent by the slices that landed them.

readiness.boundary: Starting event: the newline submitting `levelchange` at the `#` prompt, and the `>` accepted on a down staircase. Ending events: the `Welcome to experience level N.` top line with the status line the flush repaints beside it and the next command prompt; and the D:2 arrival screen with `Xp:1/2`. The real game executes both paths: `js/cmd.js` doextcmd() dispatches `#levelchange` into `js/wizcmds.js wiz_level_change()`, and `js/do.js goto_level()`'s isNew arm runs the Tourist grant. Five recorded development sessions replay the first path and gained 128 screens across the range.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch and helper reachable before the ending events was traced against nethack-c/upstream/src/: exper.c pluslvl(), more_experienced() and newexplevel(); attrib.c's fifteen innate tables, role_abil(), adjabil() and postadjabil(), setuhpmax(); wizcmds.c wiz_level_change(); botl.c xlev_to_rank() and exp_percent_changing(); weapon.c add_weapon_skill(); insight.c record_achievement() and achieve_rank(); do.c goto_level():1961-1964. The trace covered state and random-number order, including that pluslvl() prints before newhp() and newpw() draw and that postadjabil() runs after its entry's message. Explicit stops, partial implementations and missing subsystems were identified and are listed in the completeness attestation.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Every excluded branch stops before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, through a named refusal: adjabil()'s loss arm and lose_weapon_skill(); wiz_level_change()'s lowering arm behind losexp(); pluslvl(TRUE) behind newexplevel(); the Upolyd arms of pluslvl() and setuhpmax(); give_may_advance_msg(); and exp_percent_changing() with a status-highlight rule on Xp. Four excluded branches are unreachable rather than refused, each recorded with the reason: pluslvl()'s Upolyd arm and setuhpmax()'s else branch, since js/u_init.js is the port's only writer of u.umonnum; pluslvl()'s 'Welcome back' arm, since u.ulevelmax is bumped in the same block; adjabil()'s already-held suppression test, filed as a deferral against #wizintrinsic; and count_achievements() with rank_to_xlev(), whose only reader is a file the port does not write.

rejections.summary: js/allmain.js:132 -- The comments that justify the new `async` signatures state that these initializers cannot suspend, which is false for JavaScript `await`, and the false claim invites dropping an `await` that silently leaves the hero half-initialized.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comments do not claim what the finding says they claim. js/u_init.js:340-342 reads 'Asynchronous only because attrib.c adjabil() is: its gain arm can print You_feel(), which blocks on --More--. No level-1 innate entry prints, so this call awaits nothing that can suspend.' The word 'suspend' is anaphoric to 'blocks on --More--' in the preceding sentence, and under that definition the sentence is true. js/allmain.js:131-132 uses the same term in the same sense. 'suspend' is used nowhere in js/ in the microtask sense (grep -rn suspend js/ returns only these two lines, js/hack.js:1887 about notices, js/allmain.js:859 about occupations, and the extcmdlist row for ^Z), so no in-repo convention makes the strict reading natural. Counter-evidence: js/u_init.js:340-342 defines its own term one clause earlier: 'its gain arm can print You_feel(), which blocks on --More--. No level-1 innate entry prints, so this call awaits nothing that can suspend.'

rejections.summary: js/attrib.js:244 -- UnsupportedAbilityChangeError's own doc says every throw site changes an intrinsic while the hero is playing, but two of its three sites do not, and cmd.js repeats the incomplete claim by attributing all of them to adjabil()'s lowering arms.
rejections.counterEvidence: The impact rests on setuhpmax() raising this class on the raising path, and it cannot. js/exper.js:192 calls setuhpmax(u.uhpmax + hpinc, true, state), and js/attrib.js:434 guards the throw with `if (!Upolyd(u) || even_when_polyd)`; with even_when_polyd true the else arm is unreachable for that call regardless of Upolyd, and the decided non-issues already record Upolyd as false for every hero the port can build. The class is therefore reachable only from adjabil()'s two arms, exactly what js/cmd.js:918-922 describes, so no wrong edit follows from the wording. Counter-evidence: js/exper.js:192 passes even_when_polyd = true, so js/attrib.js:434's `!Upolyd(u) || even_when_polyd` is always true on the pluslvl() path and the throw at js/attrib.js:394-397 cannot execute; the claim that 'setuhpmax() throws it from the raising path' is false.

rejections.summary: js/attrib.js:320 -- adjabil() validates its message-owner contract in the middle of the traversal, after it has already written intrinsics, so a caller that omits `env.message` gets a half-applied hero plus a raw TypeError that no refusal list catches; the invariant that licenses u_init.js's owner-less call is enforced only by a test.
rejections.counterEvidence: No caller can reach the throw. The two in-tree callers are js/exper.js:217 adjabil(u.ulevel - 1, u.ulevel, state, { message }), which always supplies an owner, and js/u_init.js:377 adjabil(0, 1, state), whose span crosses only ulevel-1 entries, every one of which has an empty gainstr (js/attrib.js:127-218). The invariant is stated at js/attrib.js:123-125, 270-274 and 346-349, the last naming the test that asserts it. A non-atomic assertion on an unreachable path is a harmless deviation. Counter-evidence: js/exper.js:217 passes { message } and js/u_init.js:377 crosses only entries with gainstr '' (js/attrib.js:127-218), so js/attrib.js:320's throw is unreachable from either caller.

rejections.summary: scripts/level-change.test.mjs:378 -- Three assertions use a bare `TypeError` matcher to stand for two different refusals that adjabil() can raise -- see_monsters()'s non-global-state guard and adjabil()'s own missing-message-owner check -- so the oracle does not say which contract each test is pinning.
rejections.counterEvidence: The three assertions are not ambiguous once their setups are traced. The see-invisible test passes `message: () => assert.fail(...)`, so typeof env.message !== 'function' is false and js/attrib.js:320's TypeError cannot fire; had the message printed, the rejection would be an AssertionError, which the TypeError matcher rejects. The postadjabil test likewise passes a collector function. In the third, adjabil(9, 10, rogue) crosses rog_abil's SEARCHING entry, which js/attrib.js:262 does not dispatch on, and the owner check throws before postadjabil() is reached, so see_monsters()'s TypeError is unreachable there. No swap of one refusal for the other is possible. Counter-evidence: scripts/level-change.test.mjs supplies a message function in both see_monsters cases, making js/attrib.js:320's TypeError unreachable, and the third case crosses SEARCHING, which js/attrib.js:262 does not dispatch on, making see_monsters()'s TypeError unreachable.

passes.evidence: Counts: 15 raw, 14 deduplicated, 12 confirmed, 12 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 4 mutants. Full correctness pass over the whole of the furniture-square-entry goal, plus the previous goal's audit-fix commit, which no pass had read. Four finders; concurrency and performance were not triggered, since the range changes no asynchronous control flow and adds no hot-path work. Both slices delete refusals rather than porting new C, so the pass was aimed at the reading behind them. Three of the twelve confirmed findings were defects in shipped behavior. A blind hero arriving on furniture or an open doorway holding an object threw a bare Error out of runSegment() and discarded the segment, because js/dungeon.js surface() ports only its ROOM and CORR arms. An altar arrival over one object aborted the segment, because dfeature_at() throws and nothing on the movement path converts it. And --areas, added by the previous pass's own fix, was rejected by the recorder because the option name never entered the allowed set, while its function was tested directly and passed. All twelve applied at 9b7333e with the development score unchanged at 676 of 7,765 screens; the structural half of the second defect is deferred as movement-path-has-no-failclosed-wrapper.

optionalFinders.concurrency: not enabled: the range changes no asynchronous or reentrant control flow, no shared mutable lifecycle, and adds no parallel work; both slices delete refusals from synchronous destination predicates
optionalFinders.performance: not enabled: the range adds no unbounded or amplified work, no worse complexity and no hot-path traversal beyond the source behavior it ports

productionDefects.summary: Deleting the terrain-feature guard exposed invent.c look_here()'s blind arm, whose dungeon.c surface() port answers ROOM and CORR alone and throws a bare Error otherwise. A blind hero arriving on any furniture square or open doorway holding an object escaped js/jsmain.js's boundary list and discarded the whole segment. OPTIONS=blind reaches this from turn one.

dfeature_at() throws UnsupportedFeatureDescriptionError for an altar, and nothing on the movement path converts it: domove() has no failClosedCommand() wrapper. An altar arrival over one object aborted the segment instead of ending on its last matching screen. The reachable case is refused at the seam; the general gap is deferred as movement-path-has-no-failclosed-wrapper.

passAreas() read options.areas, but preparePass() never added the name to its allowed set, so rejectUnknownOptions() killed the command before the branch could run. The option was documented and its function tested directly, so the dead branch shipped green.

mutation.finderConclusion: Four mutants over the audit-fix diff, all killed. The two guards added to js/hack.js are pinned by new case tables that were each watched failing: removing the blind guard and removing the altar guard each fail their own test, and narrowing the pet-swap decor predicate from IS_FURNITURE to FOUNTAIN fails the widened seven-type table. No survivor needed an equivalence argument.

rejections.summary: js/hack.js:892 -- The pet-swap destination list is described as "the same set requireSimpleHeroDestination() admits above, less the doorway masks", while the code admits a doorway whose mask is 0 -- and D_NODOOR is 0, so a doorway is admitted. The sibling seam writes the same test as `mask === D_NODOOR` (js/hack.js:625-626); this one writes a bare literal.

Counter-evidence: The full sentence at js/hack.js:891-894 reads '... the same set requireSimpleHeroDestination() admits above, less the doorway masks: a D_ISOPEN swap has no recording behind it and this seam has never carried one, so it keeps the mask-0 test it was written with.' rejections.summary: js/display.js:3328 -- _stat_update_time()'s `rendered ? … : statusLayouts()` fallback performs a complete status recompute — exactly the whole-bot() behavior timebot()'s comment nine lines above says C never takes — under a header that says the function "refreshes blstats[BL_TIME] alone".
rejections.counterEvidence: The description of what the fallback does is accurate, but the hazard it rests on is not. The finding says the unreachability argument "rests on ordering that nothing enforces"; the ordering is in fact enforced twice over. Counter-evidence: js/allmain.js:141-142 (newgame_pre_mklev) sets g.disp.botlx = true before mklev, and js/moveloop_preamble.js:69 sets state.disp.botlx = true unconditionally, outside the `if (!resuming)` block, so it fires on resumed segments too. js/display.js:3201 gives the `botl || botlx` arm priority over the time_botl arm, and bot() assigns game._renderedStatusLayouts at js/display.js:3275 before clearing botl/botlx at 3276-3278. Every writer of disp.time_botl -- js/allmain.js:527, js/hack.js:372 and js/hack.js:1628 -- runs inside the moveloop, after both botlx writers. So reaching the timebot arm requires botl and botlx to be false, which requires a prior bot(), which sets _renderedStatusLayouts. The fallback cannot execute. The finding's secondary charge, that the arm "neither clears disp.botl/disp.botlx", describes correct porting rather than a defect: botl.c timebot() (293) clears only disp.time_botl.

rejections.summary: js/hack.js:678 -- The comment introducing the blind-terrain guard enumerates dungeon.c surface()'s per-terrain answers and omits THRONE and SINK, which C answers with the already-ported word "floor" through IS_ROOM(), not with a word of their own.
rejections.counterEvidence: The comment does not omit THRONE and SINK; it states their answer. Counter-evidence: js/hack.js:679-681 reads "answers per terrain: \"altar\", \"headstone\", \"fountain\", \"stairs\", \"doorway\", \"floor\" in a room and \"ground\" otherwise". The clause "'floor' in a room" is precisely dungeon.c:1783's `IS_ROOM(levtyp) && !Is_earthlevel(&u.uz)` arm, and rm.h:126 `#define IS_ROOM(typ) ((typ) >= ROOM)` with THRONE=29 / SINK=30 (rm.h:85-86) is exactly how those two types reach it, so the comment already gives them their C word rather than implying a missing one. The list is plainly a summary of the arms this guard can reach and not a per-type catalogue: it also names none of surface()'s "maw", "husk", "air bubble", "cloud", "air", "water", "bottom", "ice", "lava", "bridge" or "wall" arms, and it cites dungeon.c (1750-1787) for the full function.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:2514 -- `_optionalStatusFieldList()` joins two pre-existing helpers whose names already overlap: `_optionalStatusFields()` returns a joined string, `_optionalStatusEntries()` returns `{field, text}` records,
rejections.counterEvidence: The naming overlap is real, but the harm mechanism the finding rests on is impossible. Counter-evidence: The finding claims substituting `_optionalStatusFields()` into a `fields.push(...)` site "produces one unowned blob ... which no type check and no throw catches". It throws. `_optionalStatusFields()` returns a plain string; whether pushed whole or spread into characters, the resulting element has `field.text === undefined`, and js/display.js:2612 (`row.write(nominal, field.text, field.owner)`) reaches `_newStatusRow()`'s `write` at 2405, which evaluates `text.length` on undefined and raises a TypeError before any cell is written. The same is true of the `_writeStatusFields()` path at 2546-2547. There is no silent wrong-shape outcome to guard against.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:2744 -- The sibling builders `_statusLine2Fields()` and `_statusLine3DetailsFields()` return different shapes — a bare array versus `{ fields, hungerX }` — and the missing `hungerX` silently changes `_conditi
rejections.counterEvidence: The stated impact depends on the omission being undetected; it is detected loudly, by three existing tests including two on the whole-pass path. Counter-evidence: I applied the finding's own mutation in an isolated copy of the tree — dropping `hungerX` from `_statusLine3DetailsLayout()`'s call to `_renderStatusFields()` (js/display.js:2782), which is equivalent to dropping it from `_statusLine3DetailsFields()`'s return — and ran the full suite. Three tests fail beyond the four environment-only baseline failures: 'initial three-line status preserves tty overlap until the forced refresh', 'status uses source attribute order and exceptional strength text' (whose assertion at scripts/display-symbols.test.mjs:5175 pins `row(23).indexOf('Deaf') === row(22).length + 1`), and 'a turn-counter refresh leaves the conditions where a whole pass does'. Two of those three are whole-pass tests, contradicting the finding's claim that only the refresh path is covered and that the conditions move "with the suite still green".

rejections.summary: js/display.js:2799 -- The layout `_statusLine3DetailsLayout()` returns on the `initialTtyRefresh` pass pairs an overlap `text` with a `fields` list that re-renders to a different (steady) row, yet `_stat_update_time()`'s c
rejections.counterEvidence: No supported input can feed the overlap layout to `_refreshTimeField()`, so the stated impact — a whole-row repaint where C repaints only BL_TIME — is unreachable, and the finding itself concedes the trigger is 'anyone who later makes that row survive into a turn-counter tick'. Counter-evidence: js/moveloop_preamble.js:69 sets `state.disp.botlx = true` unconditionally (outside the `if (!resuming)` block, so resumed segments too) and only then sets `state.program_state.in_moveloop = 1` at line 84. js/display.js:3285-3296 and js/allmain.js:847-852 both give the `botl || botlx` arm priority over the `time_botl` arm, and js/display.js:3290-3294 computes `initialTtyRefresh` from `!game.program_state.in_moveloop`, so the first in-moveloop flush runs a steady `bot()` that overwrites `game._renderedStatusLayouts` at js/display.js:3360. Every `disp.time_botl` writer (js/allmain.js:527 and the two in js/hack.js) runs inside the moveloop, after that preamble. The overlap layout is therefore always replaced before any `timebot()`.

rejections.summary: scripts/quality-status.test.mjs:1003 -- The new `--areas` command-level test stops at `rejectUnknownOptions()` and never reaches the code that consumes the option, so the 'correct but unreachable branch' defect its comment names is only hal
rejections.counterEvidence: The test covers the defect its comment actually names, and the assertion is not vacuous for it. Counter-evidence: The comment at scripts/quality-status.test.mjs:981-990 names the defect as the recorder rejecting `--areas`: 'passAreas() shipped correct and unreachable ... the recorder rejected the option before the branch could run, because the name was missing from the allowed set', and the added lines say 'The defect this replaced was preparePass() rejecting --areas from an inline set'. scripts/quality-status.mjs:1118 calls `rejectUnknownOptions(options, passOptionNames(kind))` as the first statement of `preparePass()`, before any other validation, so if `areas` were missing from that set the run would return 'unknown option: --areas' and the first assertion would fail. Running the test's own argv confirms the three outcomes discriminate: `['--areas','commands']` returns '--audit-metrics or --audit-metrics-file is required', `['--nosuchoption','x']` returns 'unknown option: --nosuchoption'. The 'correct but unreachable branch' the finding attributes to the comment is the rejection, not a silently ignored option.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:3443 -- `_refuseUnfittableStatusRow(cached, refreshed)` takes two whole field arrays, but its parameter names are the same two identifiers its only caller uses, twenty lines below, for two
rejections.counterEvidence: The stated impact is not material: it is a parameter-naming and comment-placement concern, and the concrete failure mode claimed is refuted by the code as written. Counter-evidence: The finding claims a reviewer 'will bind the names to the single BL_TIME field and conclude the guard measures one field's text ... i.e. that the guard is dead'. _rowWidth is defined immediately above the guard at js/display.js:3439-3441 as `function _rowWidth(fields) { return fields.reduce((total, { text }) => total + text.length, 0); }`, so both call sites inside the guard body (`_rowWidth(refreshed)`, `_rowWidth(cached)`) show on the same screen that the arguments are field lists, not single fields. No scrolling to the call site is needed, and the guard cannot be read as dead. Behavior is unchanged either way.

rejections.summary: js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1191 -- `d.consumed` carries two unrelated contracts -- C's `bp - origbp` bookkeeping and the port-only "the player typed a qualifier" boundary signal -- and neither comment mentions the o
rejections.counterEvidence: The omission is correct rather than accidental, the guard order makes it harmless, and both claimed failure scenarios are refuted by adjacent code. Counter-evidence: cnt cannot belong to a list of 'fields that must still equal their readobjnam_init() value': js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1270-1271 (C objnam.c:4928-4929) runs `if (!d.cnt) d.cnt = 1;` unconditionally before requireUnqualifiedWish() is called at 1275, so the init value 0 is always overwritten and any such test would refuse every wish. The first claimed misreading ('counted wishes are already supported') requires ignoring the d.consumed test that is the first line of the same function the field list belongs to. The second sub-claim is wrong on its own terms: a leading count IS one of readobjnam_preparse()'s arms (objnam.c:3984-3990, the `digit(*d->bp)` branch), so the message 'the "2" qualifier' sends the reader to preparse, the correct block, not to the wrong one.

productionDefects.summary: readobjnam()'s spe switch sent TOWEL, SKELETON_KEY, HEAVY_IRON_BALL and IRON_CHAIN to its default arm, which assigns d.spe, where objnam.c:5133-5146 gives TOWEL an arm assigning only d.wetness and the other three a bare break. Harmless while a nonzero d.spesgn was refused; 517f5fb stopped refusing it, so `+2 towel` produced spe 2 and js/objnam.js:304-305 renders that as "moist towel" where C prints "towel". Fix: Ported C's TOWEL arm and the bare-break group; rewrote the default arm's comment, which had claimed the default handles those four correctly.

The count guard ran before readobjnam_postparse1(), which is where d.cnt is settled: objnam.c:4408 doubles it for "pair of " and 4423-4433's makesingular() block raises it from 1 to 2. So "daggers" reached hold_another_object() with quan 2 and ran the stack line the port declares unverified, and the range widened the hole, since "the daggers" was refused at a00741d0 and admitted at 223e9079. Fix: Moved the refusal into requireSingleWishedObject(), after typfnd:, testing both operands objnam.c:5071-5083 reads. The count alone is the wrong test, because the tail leaves quan at 1 for a type that does not merge, so "pair of speed boots" must still be admitted. Reading oc_merge costs one draw, C's own lookup at C's position, with none after it.

The SCR_MAIL arm was absent, so a wished-for scroll of mail took the default arm and was created with the enchantment the wish asked for rather than objnam.c:5168-5174's spe 1. The deferral recorded in this range justified the absence on a false premise, that no config or patch defines MAIL_STRUCTURES. Fix: Ported the arm. include/global.h:430 defines MAIL_STRUCTURES unconditionally and global.h reaches the build through hack.h; include/objects.h gates the SCR_MAIL row on the same macro and js/objects.js carries it at SCR_MAIL = 364, which is the port's own proof the comparison build compiles both. The deferral is closed and its two narrative copies corrected in place.

The module header added in this range stated that js/objnam_readobjnam.js "calls back here for the naming helpers above". Neither file imports the other. Fix: Replaced the clause with the real dependency: that file reaches the objects[] tables through js/objects.js OBJ_NAME() and OBJ_DESCR(), and object construction through js/obj.js. Verified by grep in both directions.

mutation.finderConclusion: The one survivor, `&&` to `||` in the case SCALE_MAIL arm's own PM_GRAY_DRAGON..PM_YELLOW_DRAGON test, stands. The refusal in front of the parse chain admits no monster outside that range, so both operands hold for every wish that reaches the arm, and --whole-suite over all 146 test files did not kill it either. The line is kept because C has it and it begins doing work the moment that refusal widens. The finder's separate conclusion was that the surviving risk lay not in mutable operators but in lines no test reached at all: the `if (d.spesgn === 0)` branch, the uncursed arm's `blessed = false`, and 24 of the 27 UNSUPPORTED_WISH_FIELDS entries. It says "Four arms between the direction prompt and confdir() stop rather than run" — a true statement about the four arms — and never claims to enumerate every unported expression in use_stethoscope(). passes.evidence: Counts: 17 raw, 15 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 14 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 434 survivors of 507 mutants. Full correctness pass over the monsters deferral sweep and the first options slice. Four production defects, all applied. The sharpest was count_bind_keys(), which counted every BIND statement where C's cmdbind_add() overwrites in place: two binds of one key printed '(2 currently set)' against C's 1, reproduced and then pinned by a fresh three-segment differential whose bind-keys row now agrees with C. The other three shared one habit rather than being three slips: each justified a hard-coded answer by reasoning from the port's own parser gap as though it were evidence about C, so the fixes replace guesses with refusals and teach parseNethackrc() to record the statements it drops. One finding's preferred fix was declined as out of scope and applied as a refusal instead: routing applyBooleanOption()'s fallback through booleanOptionStorage() would activate about 47 options the parser currently drops, each with a live consumer, which is a state-owner change belonging to implementation. Applying the findings also corrected two of them: C's parsebindings() recurses into the comma suffix before handling the head, so the reviewer's second bind case was wrong, and optlist.h's negateok column makes sortloot's negation a stop rather than an ignored argument. Development score identical before and after at 1,043 of 7,765 screens and 116,207 of 610,816 PRNG values; suite 2,856 green. The mutation figure needs its recorded caveat: 425 of 434 survivors are in the generated table, which the runner does not exclude.

productionDefects.summary: js/cmd.js count_bind_keys() counted every `bind` operation, where C’s cmdbind_add() overwrites in place and keeps one entry per key, so two BIND statements for one key printed "(2 currently set)" against C’s "(1 currently set)". Both loops now read the createCommandBindingModel() bindings, which replay with C’s semantics, and the model gained C’s userbind flag. This also fixed the command(param) spelling, which was counted as zero.

js/options.js booleanOptionValue() read a boolean through allopt[].addr while applyBooleanOption()’s fallback wrote flags[<lowercased name>], so any boolean whose C storage name differs was read from the wrong place. Fixed by refusing when the two disagree, covering 32 divergent spellings. The finding’s preferred fix, routing the write through booleanOptionStorage(), was declined: it would activate about 47 options the parser currently drops, each with a live consumer, which is a state-owner change needing new end-to-end cases and therefore implementation rather than an audit fix.

js/options.js count_menucolors(), msgtype_count() and count_autocompletions() returned hard-coded answers justified by the port’s own parser gap rather than by C. parseNethackrc() now records a dropped MENUCOLOR, MSGTYPE or AUTOCOMPLETE statement with C’s own prefix lengths, and each count stops on its own statement instead of guessing.

js/options.js dosetEntryFormat() hard-coded doset()’s padded layout on a false premise, that menu_tab_sep is wizard-mode-only. set_wizonly governs where doset() lists an option, not whether a config file may set it, so the tab-separated form is reachable. Now refused by name, with the comment corrected.

mutation.finderConclusion: The headline survivor count is an artifact and must not be read as a coverage figure. 425 of the 434 survivors are in js/optlist_data.js, the generated options table: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs selects sites from changed lines and does not exclude declared generated outputs, so it mutated 217 table entries whose correctness comes from check:options diffing them against the C source rather than from any test. That also explains the boolean kind’s 16-of-442 figure. The real survivor list was nine, all outside the table, and it was routed to the tests finder, which traced each. The audit fixes killed eight; one remains, js/command_bindings.js setBinding()’s restBinding default, classified rather than fixed because no call omitting the argument can bind Space: extcmdlist has no row with key 0x20, the alias table has none, and resetCommandBindings() touches only direction keys and their variants. The tooling gap is worth recording separately, because every future goal that generates a table will bury its real survivors the same way.

For the options slice, the hero types m then O and seven menu pages reach the screen; seed0007-rogue-snake-swamp advances from 20 to 36 of 302 screens, which the running game executes.

The trace covered PRNG order: the menu draws no random number, and the development total is unchanged across the range. Stubs and explicit stops were enumerated: the pick loop, reset_needed_visuals(), doset_simple_menu() and get_option_value() all stop by name.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside either boundary. Each excluded branch refuses before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, and the fixes added refusals where the port had been guessing from its own gaps. Every new refusal was checked against all 34 development sessions, 45 nethackrc values, and none carries a statement or spelling any of them covers, which is why the development score is identical before and after. passes.head: 65d1bbaad98fc51489a733c31bf9122c8e3c9dd4
passes.evidence: Counts: 19 raw, 16 deduplicated, 14 confirmed, 14 applied, 0 deferred, 2 rejected, 0 unverified; mutation: 851 survivors of 977 mutants. Full correctness pass over the options goal's pick application, closed over its own fixes. Five production defects, all applied. The sharpest is a relapse: reglyph_darkroom() threw a bare Error outside failClosedCommandRefusals(), so an ordinary OPTIONS=!color plus one menu pick aborted the whole segment and discarded every screen already matched - the same failure class the monsters sweep had just removed from dosounds and artifactTouchable, reappearing in new code and reproduced end to end by the reviewer. The others: costly_spot()'s return discarded, collapsing C's if/else and dropping a branch; oc_to_str() called on a raw pickup_types string without the guard the menu applies to the same field; the ', with exceptions' clause decided from a list the port never populates; and setBooleanOptionValue() leaving a stale parse shadow that tripped the guard the previous pass added. Two findings mattered more than their labels: the tests for the relaxed vision_recalc() guard and the new vpline() hook asserted almost nothing, and those are the only two changes in the range that no recorded session pins. The fixes corrected the reviewers twice - finding [11] proposed deleting a call that is not inert once [10] is fixed, and [10]'s own proposed validation was run and found not to discriminate, so it was pinned by a unit test instead of a recipe that would have proved nothing. Development score identical per session across all 33, at 1,056 of 7,765 screens and 116,602 of 610,816 PRNG values; suite 2,903 green. The mutation headline is noise for the third pass running: 826 of 851 survivors sit in a declared generated table the runner does not exclude.

productionDefects.summary: js/display.js reglyph_darkroom() threw a bare Error, which failClosedCommandRefusals() does not list, so an ordinary `OPTIONS=!color` or `!dark_room` plus one menu pick aborted the whole segment and discarded every screen already matched, instead of stopping on the last match. Reproduced end to end by the reviewer. This is the same failure class the monsters sweep removed from dosounds and artifactTouchable, reappearing in new code. Fixed with a named UnsupportedGlyphRepairError declared beside the existing UnsupportedStatusRefreshError in the same file and listed in js/cmd.js, so failClosedCommand() rewraps it into the command boundary runSegment() already admits. The guard stayed inside reglyph_darkroom() rather than being hoisted, so C’s other two call sites keep it.

js/insight.js discarded costly_spot()’s return value, collapsing C’s if/else at insight.c:808-819 into straight-line code and silently dropping the "temporarily disabled while inside the shop" branch of the autopickup enlightenment line.

js/insight.js called oc_to_str() on flags.pickup_types without the raw-string guard the options menu applies to the same field, so a nethackrc setting pickup_types turned ^X into unreadable output. Now refused by name.

js/insight.js decided C’s ", with exceptions" clause from state.ga.apelist, which the port never populates, so the clause could never appear. Fixed by refusing on the unported AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION statement rather than by porting the parser: autopickup_exception joins UNPORTED_CONFIG_STATEMENTS and count_apes() refuses on the same input, so no deferred work was needed.

js/options.js setBooleanOptionValue() wrote only allopt[].addr, leaving parseNethackrc()’s raw copy under flags.<name> stale, which tripped the consistency guard the previous pass added on the next menu build. Fixed by deleting the parse shadow when the two storage names differ. The affected set was enumerated programmatically at 43 boolean options and each grepped for a real reader; two hits, neither on the interactive path.

mutation.finderConclusion: The headline survivor count is an artifact for the third pass running and must not be read as coverage: 826 of the 851 survivors are in js/optlist_data.js, a declared generated output whose correctness comes from check:options diffing it against the C source rather than from any test, because scripts/mutate-sites.mjs selects sites from changed lines and does not exclude such outputs. Prior runs on this goal saw the same distortion at 425:9 and 827:25. The real list was 25, and 21 of those clustered in js/options.js 3298-3365, choose_classes_menu()’s bounds arithmetic; the tests finder was asked to decide whether that density meant an unpinned region or equivalent mutants. The audit fixes then ran their own mutation over the changed lines and reported 0 survivors of 14, having killed four that could have been excused as unreachable — including both menuinvertmode arms in js/windows.js — with direct unit tests rather than arguments.

readiness.boundary: The hero types m then O, commits nine picks from the seven-page menu, and the eight booleans plus the pickup_types class menu apply. seed0007-rogue-snake-swamp advances from 36 to 49 of 302 screens, which the running game executes.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch reachable before that ending was traced against nethack-c/upstream: options.c doset()’s pick loop, parseoptions()’s do_set path, optfn_boolean()’s do_set arm, optfn_pickup_types(), handler_pickup_types(), reset_needed_visuals(), determine_ambiguities(), match_optname() and string_for_opt(); windows.c choose_classes_menu() and menuitem_invert_test(); drawing.c def_char_to_objclass(); botl.c status_initialize(); vision.c vision_recalc()’s control == 2 fall-through; pline.c vpline() 266-271; and wintty.c tty_display_nhwindow()’s NHW_MENU arm. The trace covered PRNG order: the goal added 395 random-number calls, all from the class menu, and no other session moved.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Each excluded branch refuses before changing state, consuming randomness or producing output, and this pass fixed the one refusal that did not — reglyph_darkroom()’s bare Error. Two fresh differentials against the patched C reference cover the range, the second re-recorded during the fixes to discriminate the menuinvertmode correction end to end: 4 segments with 9,364 PRNG calls and 54 screens, and 6 rounds with 137 screens. The goal fell one step short of its 30-step forecast on a single cell’s colour at step 49, whose cause is display.c newsym()’s out-of-sight memory-correction block, reached from movement and therefore outside this boundary.

rejections.summary: js/display.js:1943 (readability) — `reglyph_darkroom()`'s guard tests that `dark_room` and `color` are currently both true, but its message says the map was "remembered under different" settings, and neither the guard nor the header comment mentions that C's trailing assignment has an else arm the port drops.
rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The two sub-claims do not hold up against the source. (a) The guard `if (!state.flags?.dark_room || !state.iflags?.wc_color) throw` (js/display.js:1943) is the exact De Morgan negation of C's condition at display.c:1850, so C's else arm at display.c:1852-1853 is refused, not silently dropped; a reviewer diffing the two sees the throw sitting where the else would run. (b) The header comment already states the test in current-value terms -- 'this refuses the two option values that would give it work' -- so the finding's claim that the comment 'describes a change, not the current-value test' misreads it. The message's 'remembered under different settings' wording is loose but is a refusal label for a state the comment above explains in full (the loop finds work only when one of the two options has moved since the square was drawn). Counter-evidence: js/display.js:1943 guard Do not reopen without a source-reachable input and a diff-causal line.

A maintainer reading the pair is told exactly what the finding says the comment conceals, so the readability claim in its own category is not supported. What is real here is the behavioral asymmetry, which is finding [7]. passes.head: eed732b3175f7b50bbe7c92dc92c4a0a881fa462
passes.evidence: Counts: 18 raw, 14 deduplicated, 12 confirmed, 12 applied, 0 deferred, 1 rejected, 1 unverified; mutation: 0 survivors of 20 mutants. Full correctness pass over the twoweapon-command goal, closed over its own fixes. Its sharpest finding was against the goal record rather than the code: the boundary and detail cited dotwoweapon() as 845-905 and can_twoweapon() as 761-833, where the spans are 843-864 and 760-804. Line 905 is the head of untwoweapon(), so the bad span attributed untwoweapon() and drop_uswapwep() to this goal - the two functions its own open deferral records as unported, which a later selector would have read as done. The other production defects: the ADMITTED_COMMANDS comment named M-2 as the command's own key when its key is X and M-2 the alias; obj.h carried() became a sixth duplicate port and was converged; and two live fail-closed boundaries were unpinned, the newly reachable Dual-weps status field and both update_inventory() calls, the first now pinned by a fresh C recording rather than an assertion. Applying the findings corrected three of them, one materially: the reviewer justified an unreachable arm by saying no role starts with a launcher in a wield slot, but the human Ranger takes a dagger primary and a bow secondary; the arm is unreachable because wield.c:765 refuses that role monster one arm earlier, verified by replaying all thirteen roles. Score bit-identical per session at 1,081 of 7,765 screens and 116,787 of 610,816 PRNG values, which is the required outcome for a range no development session can reach; the evidence is the differential, now fourteen fresh C segments at 42,032 PRNG calls and 243 screens. Mutation was clean for the first time in this sequence - 20 of 20 killed, no generated-table noise - so the tests finder judged whether tests pin behavior instead of triaging survivors, which produced five of the twelve findings.

productionDefects.summary: The goal record’s own C citations were wrong, and the error was material. `boundary` and `detail` gave `dotwoweapon() (845-905)` and `can_twoweapon() (761-833)`; the spans are 843-864 and 760-804. Line 905 is the head of `untwoweapon()`, so the bad span attributed `untwoweapon()` and `drop_uswapwep()` to this goal — the two functions the open deferral `twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms` records as NOT ported. A later selector reading the boundary would have concluded they were done. Corrected in ce65d2f by direct edit, since goal-log.mjs offers no amend for an open goal’s boundary.

The ADMITTED_COMMANDS comment said `#twoweapon`’s "own key is M-2". Its own key is `X` (cmd.c:1913, extcmdlist row 0x58); M-2 is the alias commands_init() adds at cmd.c:2776, and the port binds both. A reader auditing the boundary would have concluded `X` was already handled.

`obj.h carried()` became a second live named port: `js/obj.js:675` exported, added by this range, beside the module-private `js/eat.js:598` with an identical body. The sixth duplicate port found in this repository in two days. Converged on js/obj.js, which obj.h names; js/eat.js repointed and the private copy deleted, with the development score verified bit-identical per session.

Two live fail-closed boundaries were unpinned: `set_twoweap(true, …)` makes js/display.js’s "Dual-weps" status field reachable for the first time, and both `update_inventory({ state })` calls in dotwoweapon() could be deleted with the whole suite still green, though under `OPTIONS=perm_invent` each is the port’s only stop. The status field was pinned by a new C recording rather than a unit assertion.

mutation.finderConclusion: The first clean mutation signal of this goal sequence: 20 of 20 killed, no survivors, no timeouts, and no declared generated output in range, so none of the distortion that made the three previous passes report 425, 827 and 826 meaningless survivors applies here. With no survivor list to triage, the tests finder was asked instead to sample-verify the claim that eighteen mutation-invisible lines had each been broken with their covering test observed to fail. That reframing produced five of the twelve findings, all of them gaps a survivor list could not have shown: an untested refusal-class registration, a matrix test re-asserting a constant copied from a few lines away, an unpinned `state.flags.female` guard, and a setuwep test covering three of its expression’s terms. The audit fixes added no mutable site of their own, so their evidence runs the other way: each new assertion was shown killing a specific mutant on already-committed lines.

readiness.boundary: The hero issues `#twoweapon`. On the success path the command prints "You begin two-weapon combat.", sets `u.twoweap`, refreshes inventory and spends or does not spend the move on one `rnd(20) > ACURR(A_DEX)`; on a refusal it prints one of seven messages and spends nothing. `seed0107-samurai-twoweapon-enhance` executes the success path in the running game, advancing from 15 to 40 of 98 screens.
readiness.sourceReview: Every branch reachable before those endings was traced against nethack-c/upstream: wield.c dotwoweapon() (843-864), can_twoweapon() (760-804) with all eight of its arms, set_twoweap(), drop_uswapwep() and the TWOWEAPOK() macro; mondata.h could_twoweap(); objnam.c yname(), Yname2() and is_plural(); shk.c shk_your(), shk_owns() and mon_owns(); obj.h carried() and is_weptool(); u_init.c ini_inv_use_obj() and the role inventory tables. The trace covered PRNG order: the command draws exactly one random number on the success path and none on any refusal, which the differential confirms.
readiness.completeness: No known unsupported behavior remains inside the boundary. Three arms stay unported with derivations recorded in code and tracked as `twoweapon-unreachable-refusal-arms`, and applying the findings corrected one of those derivations: the reviewer said no role starts with a launcher in a wield slot, but the human Ranger takes a dagger primary and a bow secondary (u_init.c:124-128). The arm is still unreachable, for the different reason that wield.c:765 refuses the Ranger and Caveman role monsters one arm earlier — verified by replaying all thirteen roles. The differential grew from twelve to fourteen fresh C segments: 42,032 PRNG calls, 243 screens, all matching.

rejections.counterEvidence: evidence refute: The comment does not make the claim the finding attributes to it. Counter-evidence: js/shk.js:497-500 reads: "Its two corpse arms are absent. Both test ismnum(obj->corpsenm), and objnam.c cxname() -- which yname() calls before this -- already stops on a corpse because corpse_xname() is unported." The precondition is explicitly attributed to yname(), by name, in the same sentence that states it; a porter of ysimple_name() reading it is told which caller supplies the guarantee, not that every caller does. The caller sentence at :493-496 is a description of what shk_your() produces in C, and it is already an incomplete list of C's callers — `grep -rn "shk_your" nethack-c/upstream/src/*.c` returns apply.c:1738/2862/2908, do_wear.c:3374-3375, objnam.c:2270/2367/2394, read.c:388, trap.c:825/839 and zap.c:1042/1181 — so it plainly is not a supported-caller contract.
